Mites: Late season (Feb-Mar) in Sindh and South Punjab. Pod borer: More in areas near cotton (Multan Bahawalpur). Whitefly: More in Sindh.

question: What pests are more severe for mustard during the Kharif season?
answer: Summer mustard (high altitude only): 1) Aphids (severe). 2) Flea beetles (seedling stage). 3) Whitefly. 4) Pod borer. 5) Mites (dry periods).

question: What pests are more severe for mustard during the Rabi season?
answer: Rabi (winter) pests: Aphids (most severe Nov-Feb). Painted bug (Dec-Feb). Flea beetles (Nov-Dec on seedlings). Whitefly (Nov-Jan in warmer areas). Pod borer (Feb-March late crop). Mites (Feb-Mar late season). Aphid population peaks in January-February.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling aphids in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Imidacloprid (Confidor) 250ml/acre. 2) Thiamethoxam (Actara) 80g/acre. 3) Acetamiprid 200g/acre. 4) Dimethoate (Rogor) 400ml/acre. 5) Malathion 500ml/acre (less toxic to pollinators - use when bees not active). 6) Natural: Neem oil (2-3 L/acre). Alternate products to avoid resistance. Spray when ETL reached (30-50 aphids/plant).

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling whitefly in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Imidacloprid 250ml/acre. 2) Pyriproxyfen (Planter) 200ml/acre (insect growth regulator). 3) Buprofezin (Applaud) 300g/acre. 4) Diafenthiuron (Polo) 300ml/acre. 5) Spirotetramat (Movento) 150ml/acre - systemic. Add mineral oil (300ml/acre) as adjuvant. Rotate modes of action. Use yellow sticky traps for monitoring.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling thrips in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Spinosad (Tracer) 80ml/acre. 2) Fipronil 400ml/acre. 3) Imidacloprid 250ml/acre. 4) Thiamethoxam 80g/acre. 5) Acetamiprid 200g/acre. Spray when thrips damage visible (silvery streaks). Early morning or evening application. Repeat after 7-10 days if needed.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling stem borer in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Stem borer is rare in mustard. If present: 1) Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre as spray. 2) Remove and destroy infested plants. Prevention: destroy crop residues after harvest.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling fruit borer/pod borer in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Emamectin benzoate 200ml/acre. 2) Spinosad 80ml/acre. 3) Chlorantraniliprole (Coragen) 60ml/acre. 4) Indoxacarb 150ml/acre. 5) Lambda-cyhalothrin (Karate) 250ml/acre. Spray at flowering and pod formation when eggs/larvae seen. Use pheromone traps for monitoring (Helicoverpa armigera).

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling leaf miner in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Cyromazine (Trigard) 150g/acre - specific for leaf miners. 2) Abamectin 200ml/acre. 3) Spinosad 80ml/acre. 4) Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre. Spray when first mines appear. Best results when larvae are small. Not usually economic in mustard.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling red spider mite in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Abamectin (Kingmit) 200ml/acre. 2) Fenpyroximate (Ortus) 250ml/acre. 3) Spiromesifen (Oberon) 300ml/acre. 4) Sulfur 80% WP 500g/acre (also controls powdery mildew). 5) Propargite (Omite) 500ml/acre. DO NOT use pyrethroids (they kill natural enemies and flare mites). Repeat after 7 days.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling cutworm/armyworm in mustard seedlings?
answer: 1) Chlorpyrifos (Lorsban) 800ml/acre - soil drench around base. 2) Lambda-cyhalothrin 250ml/acre - evening spray. 3) Carbaryl (Sevin) 400g/acre. 4) Bait: Mix 1kg bran + 10g Carbaryl + 1L water - spread in evening. Apply when cutting damage first seen. Remove weeds around field.

question: What is the recommended dose and spray schedule for pesticide application on mustard?
answer: Aphids: Spray when 30-50/plant or 20% infested. Schedule: Dec-Jan peak. Pod borer: Spray at flowering (Jan-Feb) if >5% pods infested. Painted bug: Spray at pod formation if >10 per plant. General schedule: Pre-flowering (Dec) for aphids. Use 100-120 L water/acre. Rotate pesticides every 15-20 days.

question: How should pesticides be mixed and applied correctly for mustard pest control?
answer: 1) Fill spray tank 1/3 with clean water. 2) Add required pesticide dose (measure accurately). 3) Add adjuvant/wetter if recommended. 4) Fill to full volume while agitating. 5) Calibrate sprayer for 100-120 L/acre. 6) Use flat fan or hollow cone nozzles. 7) Spray in morning (6-9 AM) or evening (4-7 PM). 8) Avoid windy/rainy conditions. 9) Clean sprayer after use.

question: What is the pre-harvest interval (PHI) for pesticides used on mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Common PHI: Imidacloprid: 14 days. Thiamethoxam: 14 days. Spinosad: 7 days. Emamectin: 14 days. Chlorpyrifos: 15 days. Lambda-cyhalothrin: 14 days. Abamectin: 14 days. For mustard oil extraction: follow minimum PHI strictly. Do not harvest before PHI.

question: What are the bio-pesticides or organic alternatives for pest control in mustard?
answer: 1) Neem oil (Azadirachtin) 1% - 2-3 L/acre for aphids whitefly. 2) Garlic-chili extract (10g garlic + 10g chili in 1L water boil strain dilute 1:10). 3) Tobacco extract (100g tobacco in 1L water soak 24h strain) - effective for aphids but toxic. 4) Entomopathogenic fungi: Beauveria bassiana (2g/L) for aphids. 5) Spinosad (bio-origin) for caterpillars. 6) Yellow sticky traps for whitefly/aphids. 7) Release ladybird beetles for aphid control.

question: How can pheromone traps be used for pest monitoring in mustard fields?
answer: For cutworm: Use pheromone lures in delta traps (1 trap per 2 acres). For pod borer (Helicoverpa): Use sex pheromone lures (1 trap per 2 acres). Place traps at canopy height (50-70 cm). Check daily for moth catch. Spray when catch exceeds threshold (e.g. 8-10 moths/trap/night for borer). Replace lures every 4-6 weeks.

question: What safety equipment should a farmer wear while spraying pesticide on mustard?
answer: 1) Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile rubber). 2) Face shield or goggles. 3) Respirator (N95 or charcoal mask for organic vapors). 4) Long-sleeved shirt and full pants. 5) Apron or coverall. 6) Rubber boots (not cloth shoes). 7) Hat. Wash PPE after use. Never reuse empty pesticide containers. Shower after spraying.

question: What should a farmer do if accidental pesticide poisoning occurs during mustard spraying?
answer: 1) Remove person from contaminated area immediately. 2) Remove contaminated clothing. 3) Wash skin with soap and water for 15 minutes. 4) If swallowed: Do not induce vomiting (unless label says) - give water. 5) If inhaled: Move to fresh air. 6) Take pesticide container to hospital (for identification). 7) Seek immediate medical attention. 8) Call Poison Control (115 or local emergency).

question: How should pesticide resistance be managed in mustard pests in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Rotate pesticides with different modes of action (IRAC groups). 2) Do not use same pesticide group repeatedly. 3) Spray only when ETL reached (not calendar-based). 4) Use recommended doses (not sub-lethal). 5) Integrate biological and cultural controls (IPM). 6) Leave untreated refuges for susceptible pests. 7) Use pheromone traps for monitoring. 8) Avoid tank mixing unrelated pesticides.

question: When is the best time of day (morning/evening) to spray pesticide on mustard?
answer: Best time: Early morning (6-9 AM) or late evening (4-7 PM). Reasons: 1) Bees and pollinators less active (protect beneficials). 2) Temperature moderate (15-25°C) - better efficacy. 3) Less evaporation. 4) Lower wind speeds. Avoid spraying: 1) Mid-day heat (>30°C). 2) Strong wind (>15 km/h). 3) When rain expected within 6 hours. 4) When leaves are wet (dew/rain).

question: What integrated pest management (IPM) practices are recommended for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: IPM components: 1) Use resistant varieties (Raya Anmol for white rust). 2) Crop rotation (3-4 years with cereals). 3) Clean seed (certified disease-free). 4) Balanced fertilizer (no excess N). 5) Optimum plant population (avoid dense canopy). 6) Monitoring (weekly scouting). 7) Economic thresholds (spray only when needed). 8) Biological control (conserve ladybirds lacewings). 9) Selective pesticides (avoid pyrethroids). 10) Sanitation (remove crop debris).

question: How can crop rotation help reduce pests and diseases in mustard cultivation?
answer: Crop rotation breaks pest/disease cycles: 1) Mustard after cereals (wheat maize) - not after other Brassicas (cabbage canola rapeseed) to avoid white rust and Alternaria buildup. 2) Minimum 3-4 years between Brassica crops. 3) Rotate with non-host crops to reduce Fusarium wilt (persists 5+ years). 4) Reduces nematode populations. 5) Improves soil health. Sample rotation: Wheat - mustard - fallow - maize - wheat.

question: How does selection of disease-resistant mustard varieties reduce losses in Pakistan?
answer: Resistant varieties (Raya Anmol Punjab Sarson) provide: 1) 50-80% reduction in white rust severity. 2) Reduced need for fungicide sprays (saves Rs. 2000-3000/acre). 3) Higher yield (15-20 vs 8-12 maunds). 4) Better seed quality and oil content. 5) Reduced inoculum for neighboring fields. Always use resistant varieties where available.

question: What cultural practices help prevent pest attacks on mustard?
answer: 1) Timely sowing (Nov 1-15) - avoids peak aphid season. 2) Avoid excess nitrogen (lush growth attracts aphids). 3) Proper spacing (30-45 cm) - air circulation reduces white rust and powdery mildew. 4) Weed control (weeds host aphids and painted bug). 5) Remove crop debris after harvest. 6) Deep ploughing in summer (exposes pupae). 7) Balanced irrigation (no waterlogging). 8) Intercropping with cereals (wheat) reduces pest colonization.

question: How does field sanitation (removing crop debris) prevent disease in mustard?
answer: 1) Removes white rust-infected plant material (overwintering inoculum). 2) Reduces Alternaria and Fusarium survival structures. 3) Removes volunteer plants (alternative hosts). 4) Destroys pest hiding places. 5) Practice: After harvest collect and burn or deep plough (>30cm) mustard stubble. Do not compost infected debris. Clean cultivation equipment between fields.

question: How can border cropping or trap cropping reduce pests in mustard fields?
answer: Border crop: Surround mustard field with 2-3 rows of wheat or barley. Wheat acts as physical barrier for aphid migration. Trap cropping: Sow radish or turnip 15 days earlier on field borders. These attract painted bugs and flea beetles away from mustard. When border crop is infested spray only the border (not main crop). Reduces pesticide use by 50-70%.

question: What beneficial insects should be protected to help control pests in mustard?
answer: Beneficial insects (Friends of farmers): 1) Ladybird beetles (Coccinella) - eat aphids (up to 50/day). 2) Lacewings (Chrysoperla) - larvae eat aphids. 3) Syrphid flies (hoverflies) - larvae eat aphids. 4) Parasitic wasps (Aphidius Diaretiella) - parasitize aphids. 5) Spiders - generalist predators. 6) Ground beetles - eat cutworms. Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (pyrethroids organophosphates) to conserve them.

question: How does proper irrigation management reduce disease risk in mustard?
answer: 1) Avoid over-irrigation - reduces humidity and white rust. 2) Drip/furrow irrigation (not overhead) - keeps foliage dry. 3) Irrigate in morning - leaves dry by evening. 4) Avoid waterlogging - reduces root rot. 5) Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest - prevents late season disease. Wet foliage + cool nights = disease explosion. Proper drainage is key.

question: How does proper fertilizer management help prevent disease in mustard?
answer: 1) Balanced NPK (not excess N) - excess N causes lush growth dense canopy high humidity more white rust and aphids. 2) Adequate P and K - strengthen cell walls improve disease resistance. 3) Apply K (potassium) - reduces white rust severity. 4) Sulfur - improves oil content and plant defense. 5) Micronutrients (Zn B) - prevent stress-induced susceptibility. 6) Organic matter (FYM) - improves soil health. Soil test before fertilizer application.

question: What is the role of light traps and pheromone traps in mustard pest management?
answer: Light traps: 1) Attract night-flying pests (cutworm moths). 2) Place 1 trap per 2 acres. 3) Operate from dusk to dawn. 4) Helps monitor pest emergence. Pheromone traps: 1) Species-specific (e.g. Helicoverpa for pod borer). 2) 1 trap per 2 acres. 3) Count moths daily. 4) Spray when catch exceeds threshold. Both are monitoring tools not direct control. Reduce unnecessary sprays.

question: How should mustard fields be monitored regularly to catch pest/disease problems early?
answer: Weekly monitoring schedule: 1) Walk in W pattern across field. 2) Check 10-20 random plants per acre. 3) Aphids: Count on top 10 cm and flower buds. 4) Painted bug: Check under leaves and on pods. 5) Diseases: Check leaves for white pustules (white rust) dark spots (Alternaria). 6) Record observations (notebook/phone). 7) Use hand lens for small pests. 8) Check field borders first (pests enter from edges). 9) Monitor weather forecasts (disease risk alerts). 10) Act when thresholds reached.

question: What are the early warning signs that a mustard field needs immediate intervention?
answer: 1) Aphids: >30 per plant or sooty mold appears. 2) White rust: White pustules on >5% leaves. 3) Alternaria: Dark spots on >10% leaves. 4) Painted bug: >5 per plant or pod damage. 5) Cutworms: >5% seedlings cut. 6) Pod borer: Holes in >5% pods. 7) Wilt: Wilting plants with brown ring in stem. Don't wait - intervene immediately.

question: How does intercropping reduce pest and disease pressure in mustard?
answer: Intercropping mustard with wheat (2:4 or 2:6 ratio) reduces: 1) Aphid colonization (wheat acts as barrier and confuses aphids). 2) White rust spread (wheat reduces humidity and spore movement). 3) Painted bug (non-host crop). Intercropping pattern: 2 rows mustard + 4 rows wheat. Benefits: 25-30% reduction in pest/disease + additional income from wheat. Common practice in rainfed areas.

question: What quarantine or phytosanitary measures apply to mustard planting material in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Certified seed from Punjab Seed Corporation or provincial seed corporations is disease-tested. 2) Imported mustard/rapeseed seed requires phytosanitary certificate from country of origin. 3) Prohibited: Seed from fields with white rust or Alternaria blight. 4) Local movement: No restrictions but recommended to use disease-free seed. 5) Report unusual disease outbreaks to Department of Plant Protection.

question: What are the recommended fertilizers for mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Recommended fertilizers: 1) Nitrogen: Urea (46% N) or CAN (26% N). 2) Phosphorus: DAP (18-46-0) or SSP (18% P2O5 + 12% S). 3) Potassium: SOP (50% K2O + 18% S) or MOP (60% K2O). 4) Sulfur: SSP Gypsum (18% S) or Ammonium sulfate (24% S) - critical for oil content. 5) Micronutrients: Boron (Borax) and Zinc (ZnSO4) for deficient soils.

question: What is the recommended NPK dose per acre for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Recommended NPK: 30-40 kg N + 40-50 kg P2O5 + 20-30 kg K2O per acre. In kg/acre: N=30-40 P=40-50 K=20-30. For low fertility soils: N=45 P=55 K=35. For high fertility soils (after legumes): N=25 P=40 K=20. Sulfur: 15-20 kg S/acre. Adjust based on soil test.

question: What is the recommended dose of nitrogen (N) fertilizer for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 30-40 kg N per acre. This equals: Urea 65-85 kg (1.3-1.7 bags) per acre OR CAN 115-155 kg per acre. Apply 1/2 at sowing (basal) and 1/2 as top dressing at 30-35 days (before flowering). On rainfed: apply all N at sowing. Do not exceed 40 kg N - excess causes lodging and more disease.

question: What is the recommended dose of phosphorus (P) fertilizer for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 40-50 kg P2O5 per acre. This equals: DAP 85-110 kg (1.7-2.2 bags) OR SSP 220-280 kg per acre. Apply full dose at sowing (basal). Phosphorus is critical for: 1) Root development. 2) Flowering and pod set. 3) Oil synthesis. On P-deficient soils increase to 55-60 kg.

question: What is the recommended dose of potassium (K) fertilizer for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 20-30 kg K2O per acre. This equals: MOP 35-50 kg (0.7-1.0 bag) OR SOP 40-60 kg per acre. Apply full dose at sowing. Potassium improves: 1) Water stress tolerance. 2) Disease resistance (white rust). 3) Seed size and oil content. On sandy soils use 30-35 kg K2O.

question: When and how should the first dose of fertilizer (Basal Dose) be applied to mustard?
answer: Basal dose applied at sowing time: 1) Full P and K + 1/2 of N. 2) Apply in furrow 3-5 cm below and 2-3 cm to side of seed (drill placement). 3) If broadcasting: mix into top 5-10 cm soil during final cultivation. 4) Do not place fertilizer directly with seed (can damage germination). Use DAP (contains N+P) for basal.

question: When and how should the second and subsequent doses (Top Dressing) be applied to mustard?
answer: Top dressing: Apply remaining 1/2 N at 30-35 days after sowing (before flowering). Method: 1) Broadcast urea evenly. 2) Apply just before irrigation or light rain. 3) Avoid application when leaves are wet (causes leaf burn). 4) For rainfed: apply if good soil moisture present. No top dressing after flowering starts.

question: What is the role of sulfur (S) fertilizer in mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Sulfur is critical for mustard (oilseed crop). Role: 1) Synthesis of glucosinolates (mustard oil pungency). 2) Formation of amino acids (methionine cysteine). 3) Oil content and quality. Deficiency: pale yellow leaves stunted growth low oil content. Apply 15-20 kg S/acre as SSP (12% S) gypsum (18% S) or Ammonium sulfate (24% S). Apply at sowing.

question: What is the role of zinc (Zn) fertilizer in mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Zinc is essential for: 1) Auxin synthesis (IAA) for growth. 2) Pollen formation and seed set. 3) Oil synthesis. Deficiency symptoms: small leaves interveinal chlorosis stunted growth. Apply ZnSO4 5-8 kg/acre at sowing (mix with basal fertilizer). Foliar spray 0.3% ZnSO4 at 25-30 days for quick correction. Common in alkaline calcareous soils.

question: What is the role of boron (B) fertilizer in mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Boron is critical for: 1) Pollen tube growth and fertilization. 2) Pod formation and seed set. 3) Stem strength (prevents hollow stem). Deficiency: poor pod set hollow stems cracked stems. Apply borax (11% B) 2-3 kg/acre at sowing (mix with fertilizer). Do not exceed 4 kg - boron toxicity. Foliar spray 0.1% boric acid at bud stage. Important in sandy and alkaline soils.

question: What micronutrient deficiencies are commonly observed in mustard in Pakistani soils?
answer: Common deficiencies: 1) Sulfur (S) - most common for oilseeds (pale leaves low oil). 2) Zinc (Zn) - in calcareous soils of Punjab. 3) Boron (B) - in sandy and alkaline soils (hollow stem poor pod set). 4) Iron (Fe) - in high pH soils (interveinal chlorosis). 5) Manganese (Mn) - in organic matter deficient soils.

question: How can organic fertilizers (FYM compost Green Manure) be used for mustard cultivation?
answer: 1) FYM/compost: Apply 8-10 tons/acre 15-20 days before sowing. Mix thoroughly into soil. 2) Green manuring: Sow guar (cluster bean) or dhaincha in July-August incorporate at 50% flowering (45-50 days) - adds 40-50 kg N/acre. 3) Vermicompost: 2-3 tons/acre at sowing. Organic sources improve soil health and reduce chemical fertilizer need.

question: What is the recommended dose of farmyard manure (FYM) for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 8-10 tons (160-200 maunds) per acre. Apply well-rotted FYM (6-8 months old) 15-20 days before sowing. Spread uniformly and incorporate by cultivation. Fresh FYM should not be used (may contain weed seeds pathogens). FYM provides micronutrients improves soil structure and water holding capacity.

question: How does fertilizer application differ for irrigated vs. rainfed mustard cultivation?
answer: Irrigated: Split N (1/2 basal + 1/2 top dressing). Higher N (40 kg/acre). Full P and K at sowing. Rainfed (Barani): All N applied at sowing (no top dressing - may not activate). Lower N (25-30 kg/acre) to avoid vegetative growth exceeding moisture. Band placement for efficiency. Add extra FYM (10-12 tons) for moisture conservation. Use PSB for P availability.

question: What are the signs of nitrogen deficiency in mustard?
answer: Signs: 1) Uniform pale green to yellow leaves (starting from older leaves). 2) Stunted growth. 3) Reduced branching. 4) Small pale pods. 5) Low oil content. Remedy: apply urea 15-20 kg/acre as top dressing with irrigation.

question: What are the signs of phosphorus deficiency in mustard?
answer: Signs: 1) Dark green or purplish tint on leaves (especially underside). 2) Delayed maturity. 3) Poor root development. 4) Reduced flowering and pod set. 5) Small shriveled seeds. Remedy: apply DAP or SSP at sowing in future crops. Foliar spray 1% DAP solution (emergency).

question: What are the signs of potassium deficiency in mustard?
answer: Signs: 1) Yellowing and browning of leaf margins (scorching) starting from older leaves. 2) Weak stems prone to lodging. 3) Small pods with shriveled seeds. 4) Increased disease susceptibility (white rust). 5) Leaf curling. Remedy: apply MOP or SOP at sowing. For severe: potassium sulphate foliar spray 0.5%.

question: What are the signs of sulfur deficiency in mustard?
answer: Signs: 1) Pale yellow-green leaves (similar to N deficiency but starts on young leaves). 2) Stunted growth. 3) Thin stems. 4) Reduced oil content and pungency. 5) Delayed maturity. Remedy: apply SSP (15-20 kg S/acre) or gypsum at sowing. Sulfur is critical for oilseeds.

question: What are the signs of zinc deficiency in mustard?
answer: Signs: 1) Interveinal chlorosis (yellow between green veins) on young leaves. 2) Stunted growth with short internodes. 3) Small distorted leaves. 4) Delayed flowering. 5) Poor pod set. Remedy: ZnSO4 5-8 kg/acre soil application or foliar spray 0.3% ZnSO4 at 25-30 days.

question: What happens if too much fertilizer (over-dose) is applied to mustard?
answer: 1) Excess N: Excessive vegetative growth lodging delayed maturity poor pod set more aphids lower oil content. 2) Excess P: Induces Zn deficiency. 3) Excess K: Can cause Mg deficiency. 4) Excess fertilizer (any): Salt injury to roots leaf burn groundwater pollution wasted money. For mustard: excess N is the most common problem. Always follow recommended doses.

question: What are the recommended fertilizer products (brand names) available in Pakistan for mustard?
answer: 1) Urea: Sona Urea Engro Urea Fauji Urea. 2) DAP: Engro DAP Fauji DAP ICI DAP. 3) SSP: Pakarab SSP (good source of P and S). 4) SOP: Fauji SOP Engro SOP (for K and S). 5) MOP: Engro MOP FFC MOP. 6) ZnSO4: Fauji Zinc Engro Zinc. 7) Borax: Madak Borax. 8) Ammonium sulfate: Fauji AS (24% S).

question: How should urea be applied to mustard to avoid losses from volatilization (gas loss)?
answer: 1) Apply urea just before irrigation (within 1-2 days) or light rain. 2) Incorporate into soil by light cultivation (2-3 cm depth) if no irrigation. 3) Do not broadcast urea on dry soil without incorporation - ammonia loss up to 30%. 4) Use neem-coated urea (slower release lower loss). 5) Split application (two doses) reduces loss per application.

question: How many irrigations does mustard require in total during its growing season in Pakistan?
answer: Mustard requires 2-4 irrigations in irrigated areas. Rainfed (Barani): 0-2 supplemental irrigations if available. Irrigation schedule: 1st at 20-25 days (branching). 2nd at 40-45 days (flowering - CRITICAL). 3rd at 65-75 days (pod formation). 4th at 85-95 days (pod filling - only if needed). Mustard is drought-tolerant.

question: When should the first irrigation (Pehl-pani) be given to mustard after sowing?
answer: First irrigation at 20-25 days after sowing (branching stage). Earlier irrigation (before 15 days) may cause waterlogging and seedling damping off. Delay beyond 30 days reduces branching and yield. In rainfed areas: rely on soil moisture - irrigate only if severe drought.

question: What are the critical growth stages of mustard that require mandatory irrigation?
answer: Three critical stages: 1) Flowering stage (40-50 days) - water stress causes flower drop poor pollination reduced pod set (30-40% loss). 2) Pod formation and filling (65-80 days) - stress reduces seed size and oil content. 3) Branching stage (20-30 days) - stress reduces branches and pods. Avoid stress at these stages.

question: How many days apart should irrigations be given to mustard in summer (Kharif) in Pakistan?
answer: Summer mustard (high altitude areas only - Balochistan KPK hills): interval 10-15 days. Higher temperatures increase evapotranspiration. Light frequent irrigations (2-3 acre-inches) are better. Avoid overhead irrigation during flowering.

question: How many days apart should irrigations be given to mustard in winter (Rabi) in Pakistan?
answer: Winter irrigation interval: 20-30 days depending on soil type. Sandy soils: 15-20 days. Loamy soils: 20-25 days. Clay soils: 25-30 days. Cool temperatures (10-20°C) reduce evapotranspiration. Do not irrigate if soil already wet or frost forecast.

question: What is the total water requirement (acre-inches) of mustard per crop season?
answer: Total water requirement: 250-350 acre-inches (6-8 million liters per acre). This is equivalent to 2-4 irrigations of 3-4 acre-inches each plus effective rainfall (100-150mm). Mustard is relatively drought-tolerant compared to wheat or rice.

question: What irrigation method is suitable for mustard in Pakistan — flood furrow drip or sprinkler?
answer: 1) Furrow irrigation: Best method - saves water prevents waterlogging reduces foliar diseases. 2) Border strip/flood: Acceptable on level fields but can cause waterlogging. 3) Sprinkler: Excellent for sandy soils undulating land and frost protection - saves 25-30% water. 4) Drip: Not economical for mustard (low value crop) but works. Avoid basin flooding on heavy soils.

question: How does drip irrigation improve the water use efficiency of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Drip irrigation saves 40-50% water compared to flood but is not cost-effective for mustard (Rs. 120000-150000/acre setup cost). For high-value seed production or water-scarce areas drip allows precise water delivery reduces weed growth and prevents foliar diseases. Government 60% subsidy available.

question: How should irrigation be managed during the flowering stage of mustard?
answer: Flowering stage (40-50 days) is critical. Management: 1) Ensure adequate soil moisture - avoid water stress. 2) Light irrigation (2-3 acre-inches) rather than heavy. 3) Avoid overhead sprinkler during peak flowering (9 AM-4 PM) - can wash off pollen. 4) Irrigate in morning hours. 5) Do not irrigate if strong winds or frost expected. 6) Water stress at flowering reduces yield 30-50%.

question: How should irrigation be managed during the grain-filling or fruiting stage of mustard?
answer: Pod filling stage (70-85 days): 1) Maintain moderate soil moisture (not wet). 2) Stress at this stage reduces seed size and oil content. 3) One irrigation at 70-75 days if no rainfall. 4) Avoid over-irrigation which delays maturity and increases disease (white rust). 5) Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest for uniform ripening.

question: What are the signs of water stress (drought) in mustard and what is the immediate remedy?
answer: Signs: 1) Wilting during day (leaves droop). 2) Leaves turn dull bluish-green. 3) Stunted growth. 4) Premature flowering and small pods. 5) Flowers drop. 6) Small shriveled seeds. Immediate remedy: Apply light irrigation (2-3 acre-inches) immediately. If no irrigation available: spray water early morning (emergency).

question: What are the signs of waterlogging in mustard and how to drain excess water?
answer: Signs: 1) Yellowing of lower leaves. 2) Wilting despite wet soil. 3) Root rot (black/brown roots). 4) Plant death in patches. 5) Fungal growth on soil surface. Drainage: 1) Immediately stop irrigation. 2) Open drains/furrows to remove standing water. 3) On flat fields: make temporary channels. 4) For future: plant on raised beds or ridges.

question: How should irrigation be managed after fertilizer application to mustard?
answer: After basal fertilizer (at sowing): Irrigate within 5-7 days if no rain. After top dressing urea (30-35 days): Irrigate within 2-3 days to incorporate N and prevent ammonia loss. Apply irrigation when leaves are dry (morning). Light irrigation (2-3 inches) is sufficient - heavy irrigation leaches nutrients.

question: Should mustard irrigation be stopped before harvest? How many days before?
answer: Yes stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest. This allows: 1) Uniform ripening of pods. 2) Reduction in seed moisture content. 3) Prevention of pod shattering. 4) Easier harvesting. Late irrigation delays maturity and can cause seed sprouting in pods if rain occurs.

question: How does canal water vs. tube well (brackish/salty) water affect mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Canal water: Best for mustard - low EC (<1 dS/m) good for all stages. Fresh tube well water (EC <1.5): Acceptable. Brackish/saline tube well water (EC >2): Damages mustard - causes leaf burn reduced germination yield loss up to 40%. Mustard has moderate salt tolerance (ECe up to 6). If only saline water available: 1) Mix with canal water (1:1). 2) Apply gypsum. 3) Use salt-tolerant varieties (Sindh Raya). 4) Avoid irrigation at germination and flowering.

question: What is the average yield of mustard per acre in Pakistan?
answer: Average yield (seed): 8-12 maunds per acre (320-480 kg). Punjab (irrigated): 12-16 maunds. Punjab (rainfed Pothwar): 8-10 maunds. Sindh: 10-14 maunds. KPK: 8-12 maunds. Balochistan: 6-10 maunds. National average is below potential due to rainfed conditions diseases and traditional practices.

question: What is the maximum achievable yield (Potential Yield) of mustard per acre under best management in Pakistan?
answer: Potential yield: 25-30 maunds per acre (1000-1200 kg) under optimal conditions (improved variety irrigation balanced fertilizer pest/disease control). Research station yields: 25-28 maunds/acre. Progressive farmer yields: 18-22 maunds/acre. Yield gap between average (10 maunds) and potential (25 maunds) is 150% - large opportunity for improvement.

question: What are the main reasons for low mustard yield in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Rainfed cultivation (moisture stress) - 60% area. 2) Low-yielding traditional varieties (8-10 maunds). 3) White rust disease (20-40% loss). 4) Alternaria blight (15-30% loss). 5) Poor soil fertility (low P S OM). 6) No fertilizer use or imbalanced. 7) Aphid infestation (20-30% loss). 8) Late sowing (after Nov 30). 9) Weed competition (30-50% loss).

question: How can a farmer increase the yield of mustard from 20 maunds to 40+ maunds per acre?
answer: Mustard yield target is 25-30 maunds maximum (not 40+). To increase from 8 maunds to 20+ maunds: 1) Use improved variety (Raya Anmol Punjab Sarson). 2) Irrigated cultivation (3-4 irrigations) instead of rainfed. 3) Balanced fertilizer: 40 kg N + 50 kg P2O5 + 20 kg K2O + 20 kg S per acre. 4) Seed treatment (fungicide + insecticide). 5) Timely sowing (Nov 1-15). 6) Weed control (pre+post herbicide). 7) White rust control (2 fungicide sprays). 8) Aphid control (at ETL). 9) Proper harvest (timely low loss). These steps can triple yield.

question: How does timely sowing affect the final yield of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Each week delay after Nov 15 reduces yield by 5-10%. Nov 1-15 sowing: 15-20 maunds/acre. Nov 15-30: 12-15 maunds. Dec 1-15: 8-10 maunds. Dec 15+: 4-6 maunds. Timely sowing allows: optimum temperature during flowering (15-20°C) good pod set and higher oil content (42% vs 35%).

question: How does proper fertilizer management (Balanced use) increase the yield of mustard?
answer: Balanced NPKS (40-50-20-20 kg/acre) increases yield by 50-80% over no fertilizer. Specific gains: N (40 kg) = +40% yield (vegetative growth branching). P (50 kg) = +30% yield (root development pod set). K (20 kg) = +15% yield (stress tolerance oil content). S (20 kg) = +25% yield (oil content and pungency). Combined effect: can increase from 8 to 18 maunds/acre.

question: How does proper irrigation management increase the yield of mustard?
answer: One irrigation at flowering (40-45 days) increases yield 20-30% over rainfed. Two irrigations (branching + flowering) increase 40-50%. Three irrigations (branching + flowering + pod fill) increase 60-80%. In rainfed areas (0 irrigation): 6-8 maunds. With 3-4 irrigations: 15-18 maunds. Water is a major limiting factor.

question: What role does pest and disease control play in increasing mustard yield?
answer: White rust (uncontrolled): 20-40% yield loss + poor oil quality. Alternaria blight (uncontrolled): 15-30% yield loss. Aphids (uncontrolled): 20-30% yield loss. Combined pest/disease: can cause 70%+ loss (yield 3-4 maunds). Effective control: 2-3 fungicide sprays + aphicide at ETL = 40-60% yield protection. IPM practices save yield without excessive cost.

question: What are the best agronomic practices recommended by PARC/NARC for high-yield mustard production?
answer: PARC/NARC recommendations: 1) Variety: Raya Anmol or P-18. 2) Sowing: Nov 1-15 at 30-45 cm spacing 3-4 kg seed/acre. 3) Seed treatment: Carbendazim + Imidacloprid. 4) Fertilizer: 40-50-20-20 kg NPKS per acre. 5) Irrigation: 3-4 irrigations (branching flowering pod fill). 6) Weed control: Pendimethalin pre-emergence + one manual weeding. 7) White rust control: Metalaxyl spray at rosette stage. 8) Harvest: at 70-80% pod browning.

question: How can improved seed quality (Certified Seed) increase the production of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Certified seed provides: 1) Higher genetic purity (>98%). 2) Higher germination (85%+ vs 60-70% farm-saved). 3) Disease-free (no seed-borne Alternaria white rust). 4) True-to-type (uniform maturity plant height). 5) Yield increase: 20-30% over farm-saved seed. Cost: Rs. 150-250/kg vs farm-saved Rs. 80-120/kg. Available at Punjab Seed Corporation and progressive dealers.

question: What role does soil health improvement play in boosting mustard yield in Pakistan?
answer: Improved soil health (1.5-2.5% organic matter) boosts yield 30-50% through: 1) Better water holding capacity (critical in rainfed). 2) Higher nutrient availability (especially N P S). 3) Improved soil structure (root growth). 4) Beneficial microbes (disease suppression). 5) Reduced crusting (better emergence). Practices: FYM 8-10 tons/acre green manuring crop rotation minimum tillage.

question: How does the use of growth regulators (Plant Hormones) affect mustard yield?
answer: Not commonly used in mustard in Pakistan. Research shows: 1) Gibberellic acid (GA3) 20-40 ppm at branching - increases plant height but may cause lodging. 2) Mepiquat chloride - reduces lodging in tall varieties but not commercial. Not recommended for general use. Focus on basic agronomy first.

question: What intercropping or relay cropping strategies can increase income from mustard farming?
answer: 1) Mustard + Wheat (2:4 or 2:6 rows) - reduces pest/disease by 25% and provides wheat income (10-15 maunds/acre). 2) Mustard + Gram (1:2) - legumes fix N benefit mustard. 3) Relay cropping: Sow mustard into standing rice 15-20 days before rice harvest. 4) Mustard as catch crop after early potato. Intercropping land equivalent ratio (LER) >1.5 - more productive than sole cropping.

question: What are the top 5 things a farmer can do to double the yield of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Switch from traditional variety to Raya Anmol or P-18 (+50% yield). 2) Provide 3-4 irrigations (branching flowering pod fill) instead of rainfed (+80% yield). 3) Apply balanced fertilizer: 40-50-20-20 kg NPKS per acre (+60% yield). 4) Control white rust with 2 sprays of Metalaxyl (+40% yield protection). 5) Control aphids when threshold reached (+30% yield). Combined effect: 6-8 maunds to 18-22 maunds (2-3x increase).

question: How can precision agriculture or modern technology improve mustard production in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Laser land leveling: uniform irrigation saves water 20-30%. 2) Soil testing: precise fertilizer recommendation saves cost. 3) Drone monitoring: detect pest/disease hotspots early (available as service). 4) Variable rate technology: apply inputs based on soil variability (not common yet). 5) Mobile apps: pest scouting weather alerts market prices (e.g. AgriApp). 6) Drip irrigation (subsidized) - for high-value seed production. Adoption gradually increasing.

question: How does climate change affect mustard yield in Pakistan and how can farmers adapt?
answer: Climate change impacts: 1) Warmer winters - reduced pod set lower oil content. 2) Unpredictable rains - drought/flood. 3) Higher temperatures during pod filling - small shriveled seeds. 4) Increased pest/disease pressure (white rust aphids). Adaptations: 1) Heat-tolerant varieties. 2) Drought-tolerant varieties for rainfed. 3) Shift sowing dates (slightly earlier or later). 4) Supplemental irrigation. 5) Mulching for moisture conservation. 6) Climate-smart practices (zero-till intercropping).

question: What are the major fungal diseases (Uli) of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Major fungal diseases: 1) White rust (Albugo candida) - most important and destructive. 2) Alternaria blight (Alternaria brassicae). 3) Downy mildew (Peronospora parasitica). 4) Powdery mildew (Erysiphe cruciferarum). 5) Sclerotinia stem rot (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). 6) Damping off (Rhizoctonia Pythium) - seedlings. 7) Black leg (Leptosphaeria maculans).

question: What are the major bacterial diseases of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Bacterial diseases are rare in mustard in Pakistan. Occasional: Bacterial blight (Xanthomonas campestris) - water-soaked spots on leaves. Not economically significant. Fungal diseases are main concern.

question: What are the major viral diseases of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Viral diseases are rare. Occasional: Turnip mosaic virus (TuMV) - transmitted by aphids. Symptoms: mosaic pattern leaf distortion stunting. Control by managing aphid vectors. Not economically significant.

question: How can I identify rust disease (Kungi) in mustard fields?
answer: Rust is not a major disease of mustard. White rust (Albugo) is sometimes confused with rust but is a different pathogen. White rust symptoms: White shiny pustules (blisters) on leaves stems and flower stalks. Pustules turn brown with age. Severe: swelling and distortion of stems (staghead).

question: How can I identify powdery mildew in mustard and what causes it?
answer: Powdery mildew (Erysiphe cruciferarum). Causes: High humidity (60-80%) moderate temperatures (15-25°C) dense canopy. Symptoms: 1) White powdery coating on upper leaf surfaces (looks like flour dusted). 2) Spreads to stems and pods. 3) Leaves turn yellow then brown. 4) Premature defoliation. Appears from February onward.

question: How can I identify downy mildew in mustard and what causes it?
answer: Downy mildew (Peronospora parasitica). Symptoms: 1) Yellowish-green patches on upper leaf surface. 2) Purplish-grey fluffy growth on underside of leaves (sporangia). 3) Leaf curling and thickening. 4) Stunted plants. Favored by cool wet weather. Often occurs together with white rust.

question: How can I identify blight (early/late) in mustard and what causes it?
answer: Alternaria blight (Alternaria brassicae) - most common blight. Symptoms: 1) Small dark brown to black spots on leaves (target-like concentric rings). 2) Spots enlarge coalesce causing leaf blighting. 3) Dark sunken lesions on pods (pod spot). 4) Seed infection (shriveled discolored). Favored by warm humid weather. Spread by seed and crop debris.

question: How can I identify damping off disease in mustard seedlings?
answer: Damping off (Rhizoctonia solani Pythium spp.). Symptoms: 1) Pre-emergence: seeds rot before germination (patchy emergence). 2) Post-emergence: seedlings collapse at soil line (stem constricted dark lesion). 3) Infected patches in field. Favored by: wet cold soils poor drainage dense sowing. Control: seed treatment + avoid over-irrigation + well-drained soil.

question: What is wilt (Sokra) disease in mustard and how to identify it?
answer: Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. conglutinans). Symptoms: 1) Yellowing starting from lower leaves upward. 2) Wilting despite adequate moisture. 3) Brown discoloration of vascular tissue (cut stem cross-section shows brown ring). 4) Plants die from bottom upward. 5) Patchy distribution. Favored by warm temperatures (25-30°C) and low soil moisture. Use resistant varieties.

question: What is smut or bunt (Siyah-rooli) disease in mustard and how to identify it?
answer: Smut is NOT a significant disease of mustard in Pakistan. No economic impact. Focus on white rust and Alternaria blight as major diseases.

question: What virus diseases affect mustard in Pakistan and what are their symptoms?
answer: Occasional virus diseases: Turnip mosaic virus (TuMV). Symptoms: 1) Mosaic pattern (light and dark green patches). 2) Leaf distortion and puckering. 3) Vein clearing. 4) Plant stunting. 5) Reduced pod set. Transmitted by aphids. No direct control - manage aphid vectors.

question: How do diseases spread from one mustard plant or field to another?
answer: 1) White rust: Wind-borne sporangia seed-borne. 2) Alternaria blight: Seed-borne + rain splash + wind. 3) Downy mildew: Wind and rain splash. 4) Fusarium wilt: Soil-borne (persists years) + infected plant debris + contaminated tools. 5) Damping off: Soil + contaminated seed + irrigation water. Prevention: clean seed crop rotation disease-free debris management.

question: What weather conditions (humidity/rain) favor disease development in mustard?
answer: White rust: Cool (10-20°C) humid (>80% RH) with dew/fog. Alternaria blight: Warm (20-28°C) wet conditions (rain/high humidity). Downy mildew: Cool wet conditions. Powdery mildew: Moderate temps (15-25°C) high humidity (but no free water). Jan-Feb foggy conditions in Punjab favor white rust and Alternaria.

question: Which regions of Pakistan are most affected by mustard diseases and why?
answer: White rust: Most severe in Pothwar region (Rawalpindi Attock) and irrigated areas of Punjab due to cool humid foggy winters. Alternaria blight: Widespread but more in Sindh and South Punjab (warmer humid). Downy mildew: More in KPK and northern Punjab. Overall white rust is the #1 disease across all regions.

question: What is the difference between nutrient deficiency symptoms and disease symptoms in mustard?
answer: Nutrient deficiency: Symmetrical pattern often interveinal chlorosis uniform across field usually on older leaves first (N P K S) or young leaves (Zn Fe). No pathogen signs (no spores pustules mycelium). Corrected by fertilizer. Disease: Irregular patches pustules (white rust) white powder (mildew) dark lesions (blight) often with pathogen structures. Spreads over time. Fungicides may help.

question: What fungicides are recommended for controlling white rust in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) 400g/acre. 2) Fosetyl-Al (Aliette) 500g/acre. 3) Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (Curzate) 400g/acre. 4) Mancozeb (Dithane M-45) 500g/acre - protectant. 5) Chlorothalonil (Bravo) 500ml/acre. Apply at first sign of white pustules. Repeat after 10-14 days if needed. Use resistant varieties (Raya Anmol).

question: What fungicides are recommended for controlling Alternaria blight in mustard?
answer: 1) Mancozeb (Dithane M-45) 500g/acre - protectant. 2) Chlorothalonil (Bravo) 500ml/acre. 3) Propiconazole (Tilt) 250ml/acre. 4) Tebuconazole (Folicur) 250ml/acre. 5) Azoxystrobin (Amistar) 200ml/acre. 6) Copper oxychloride 400g/acre. Apply at early flowering stage. Repeat every 10-14 days if wet conditions persist. Use certified disease-free seed.

question: What fungicides are recommended for controlling powdery mildew in mustard?
answer: 1) Sulfur (80% WP) 500g/acre - effective cheap. 2) Tebuconazole 250ml/acre. 3) Propiconazole 250ml/acre. 4) Myclobutanil 200g/acre. 5) Hexaconazole 250ml/acre. 6) Dinocap (Karathane) 400ml/acre. Apply at first sign of white powder. Sulfur is organic-friendly but avoid when temperature >30°C.

question: What fungicides are recommended for controlling wilt in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Wilt (Fusarium) is difficult to control with fungicides once symptoms appear. Prevention: 1) Seed treatment with Carbendazim 2g/kg + Thiram 2g/kg. 2) Soil drench with Carbendazim 500g/acre (early stages). 3) Trichoderma harzianum (bio-fungicide) 2kg/acre in furrow at sowing. 4) Use resistant varieties. 5) Crop rotation (4-5 years with cereals).

question: What bactericides are used for bacterial diseases of mustard in Pakistan?
answer: Bacterial diseases are rare in mustard. If bacterial blight occurs: 1) Copper oxychloride 400g/acre. 2) Streptomycin + Tetracycline (Agrimycin) 100g/acre. Not routinely needed.

question: What is the spray schedule for disease management in mustard in Pakistan?
answer: White rust: 1st spray at rosette stage (Dec-Jan) if disease seen. 2nd spray 10-14 days later. Alternaria blight: Pre-flowering spray (Jan) if history. Powdery mildew: Spray when white powder seen (Feb). General schedule: Monitor weekly from December. Spray only when disease reaches threshold. Use protectant fungicides (Mancozeb Sulfur) before disease arrives.

question: What is the correct dose and method of fungicide application on mustard?
answer: 1) Calculate field area and required product dose. 2) Use 100-120 liters water per acre. 3) Add fungicide to water while agitating. 4) Use flat fan or hollow cone nozzles. 5) Spray to cover all leaves (upper and lower surfaces). 6) For white rust: good coverage of lower leaf surface is critical. 7) Spray in morning (6-9 AM). 8) Avoid spraying during flowering if possible (protect bees).

question: What systemic vs. contact fungicides are recommended for mustard?
answer: Systemic (absorbed by plant): Metalaxyl Tebuconazole Propiconazole Azoxystrobin - curative (can be used after infection) longer protection (10-14 days). Contact (surface only): Mancozeb Chlorothalonil Copper oxychloride Sulfur - preventive (must be applied before infection) shorter protection (5-7 days). Strategy: Use protectants early then systemics when disease appears. Alternate both to prevent resistance.

question: How often should fungicide be sprayed during the mustard growing season?
answer: Depends on disease pressure: Low pressure: 0-1 spray (only if disease appears). Moderate pressure: 2 sprays at 10-14 day interval (Dec-Jan). High pressure (white rust in Pothwar): 3 sprays (Dec Jan early Feb). Do not exceed 3 sprays to avoid resistance and cost. Stop spraying after pod filling stage (90 days).

question: What are the bio-fungicides or organic disease control methods for mustard?
answer: 1) Sulfur (organic approved) for powdery mildew. 2) Neem oil (0.5%) for mildew and rust suppression. 3) Baking soda (1%) + vegetable oil (0.5%) for powdery mildew. 4) Trichoderma harzianum (2kg/acre) soil application for wilt control. 5) Cow urine (10% solution) as foliar spray (traditional). 6) Crop rotation (3-4 years). 7) Resistant varieties (Raya Anmol).

question: When is mustard ready for harvest in Pakistan?
answer: Mustard is ready for harvest in March to April (110-145 days after sowing). Punjab: March 15 to April 15. Sindh: March 1-31. KPK: April 1-30. Balochistan: April-May (spring crop) or August-September (summer crop). Harvest when 70-80% of pods turn yellow-brown and seeds rattle inside.

question: What are the visual signs that mustard has reached maturity and is ready to harvest?
answer: 1) Pods: 70-80% yellow-brown to brown. 2) Seeds: Rattle inside when shaken. 3) Stems: Turn yellow-brown. 4) Leaves: Most have dropped. 5) Seeds: Hard shiny black or yellow (depending on variety). 6) Moisture content: 20-25% in seeds. Do not delay - over-ripe pods shatter causing seed loss.

question: What is the recommended moisture content of mustard at time of harvest?
answer: Harvest at 20-25% seed moisture content. At this stage: 1) Seeds are mature but not too dry. 2) Minimal shattering during harvest. 3) Can be manually cut without excessive loss. After harvest dry to 8-10% moisture for storage. Use moisture meter or traditional method (bite test - hard).

question: How is mustard harvested in Pakistan — manually (Daranti) or mechanically?
answer: Manual harvesting (dominant): 1) Using daranti (sickle) to cut plants close to ground. 2) Plants tied in small bundles (sheaves). 3) Stacked in field for 5-7 days drying. 4) Threshing by beating or bullock trampling. Mechanical: Combine harvester (increasing adoption) - cuts threshes and cleans in one operation. Also use reaper (cuts only) + thresher. Mechanical reduces labor cost but may cause more shattering.

question: What machinery (Combine Harvester/Thresher) is used for harvesting mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Combine harvester (e.g. New Holland John Deere) - for large fields (>5 acres). Settings: Cylinder speed 400-500 RPM concave clearance wide to avoid seed cracking. 2) Reaper (tractor-mounted) - cuts plants into windrows then pick up with thresher. 3) Stationary thresher - for manually harvested bundles. 4) Manual beating - on tarpaulin (traditional). Hire combine service: Rs. 2500-3500/acre.

question: How should mustard be harvested to minimize shattering or field losses?
answer: 1) Harvest at 70-80% pod browning (not fully dry). 2) Harvest early morning when dew present (pods less brittle). 3) Use sharp sickles (clean cut reduces shatter). 4) Handle bundles gently - don't shake. 5) For combine: reduce cylinder speed (400-500 RPM). 6) Keep header low (5-10 cm above ground). 7) Harvest promptly - don't leave over-ripe in field. 8) Losses can be 15-25% if mismanaged.

question: What is the correct harvesting time for mustard in Punjab?
answer: Punjab: March 15 to April 15. Central Punjab (Sargodha Faisalabad Gujranwala): March 20-April 10. South Punjab (Multan Bahawalpur): March 15-30. North Punjab (Rawalpindi Attock): April 1-20.

question: What is the correct harvesting time for mustard in Sindh?
answer: Sindh: March 1 to March 31. Upper Sindh (Sukkur Jacobabad): March 10-31. Lower Sindh (Hyderabad Mirpurkhas): March 1-20. Warmer climate leads to earlier harvest.

question: What is the correct harvesting time for mustard in KPK?
answer: KPK: April 1 to April 30. Peshawar valley: April 5-25. Dera Ismail Khan: March 25-April 15. Higher elevations (Swat Abbottabad): May-June (spring crop).

question: What is the correct harvesting time for mustard in Balochistan?
answer: Balochistan: Two seasons. Plains (Sibi Naseerabad): March 15-April 15 (winter crop). Highlands (Quetta Pishin): June-July (spring crop). Summer crop: August-September.

question: What post-harvest activities are done immediately after mustard harvest?
answer: 1) Drying: Spread in sun for 5-7 days until seeds rattle (8-10% moisture). 2) Threshing: Beating bundles or machine thresher. 3) Winnowing: Separate seeds from chaff using wind or fan. 4) Cleaning: Remove dust stones immature seeds. 5) Drying again: If moisture >10% - sun dry 1-2 more days. 6) Bagging: Clean jute/plastic bags. 7) Storage: Cool dry place.

question: How long after sowing is mustard typically harvested in Pakistan?
answer: 110-145 days after sowing depending on variety and climate. Early varieties (P-18): 100-110 days. Medium (Raya Anmol Punjab Sarson): 115-125 days. Late (Sindh Raya): 130-145 days. Rainfed conditions may extend by 5-10 days.

question: What are the common mistakes farmers make during mustard harvesting in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Harvesting too early (green pods) - immature seeds low oil content. 2) Harvesting too late (over-ripe) - shattering loss up to 30%. 3) Cutting too high - leaving lower pods in field. 4) Rough handling - causes seed shattering. 5) Not drying properly - mold in storage. 6) Threshing on bare ground - mixing with soil/stones. 7) Using combine at wrong settings - cracked seeds. 8) Mixing varieties - inconsistent quality.

question: How should mustard be stored after harvest in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Dry seeds to 8-10% moisture (sun dry 5-7 days). 2) Clean thoroughly (remove weed seeds debris). 3) Store in clean dry jute bags or hermetic (PICS) bags. 4) Stack bags on wooden pallets (not direct floor). 5) Maintain cool dry well-ventilated store. 6) Treat with neem leaves or camphor for insects. 7) For long-term: fumigate with aluminum phosphide (2-3 tablets/ton) - use trained person. 8) Monitor monthly for moisture/pests.

question: What is the ideal moisture content of mustard for safe long-term storage?
answer: 8-10% moisture content for safe storage up to 12 months. Above 10%: risk of mold and insect damage. Above 12%: rapid deterioration. Below 8%: excessive seed cracking. Use moisture meter. Traditional test: bite seed - should be hard and crisp.

question: What are the major post-harvest losses for mustard in Pakistan and how to reduce them?
answer: Major losses: 1) Shattering during harvest (15-25%). Reduce: timely harvest gentle handling. 2) Incomplete threshing (5-10%). Reduce: proper threshing setting. 3) Bird damage (5-15% if left in field). Reduce: harvest promptly. 4) Storage insects (10-20% over 6 months). Reduce: dry seed proper storage fumigation. 5) Mold (5-15%). Reduce: dry to <10% moisture. Total losses can exceed 40% without proper management.

question: What storage structures or containers are recommended for mustard in rural Pakistan?
answer: 1) Metal bins (drum) - airtight rodent-proof best option. 2) Hermetic bags (PICS or GrainPro) - prevents insect entry no fumigation needed. 3) Jute bags (gunny) - with inner polythene liner. 4) Clay bins (Godaym) - traditional seal with mud. 5) Plastic silos (govt scheme). Avoid: direct floor storage old chemical bags damp rooms.

question: What pest control measures should be taken during mustard storage?
answer: 1) Clean storage area before filling. 2) Dry seeds to 8-10% moisture. 3) Mix neem leaves (1kg/100kg seed) or dried neem powder. 4) Use food-grade diatomaceous earth (1kg/ton) - physical insecticide. 5) Fumigation: Aluminum phosphide tablets (2-3 per ton) - only by trained person. 6) Pheromone traps for monitoring. 7) Inspect monthly for webbing live insects musty smell. 8) Never mix old with new grain.

question: What fumigants or storage pesticides are recommended for mustard in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Aluminum phosphide (Phostoxin) - 2-3 tablets per ton. CAUTION: Highly toxic - use trained fumigator only. Seal storage for 5-7 days. Aerate 48 hours before use. 2) Malathion dust (2% active) - 250g per ton (mix with seed). 3) Deltamethrin dust - as label. For small quantities: neem leaves camphor. Never consume treated seeds for oil extraction.

question: How long can mustard be stored without significant quality loss?
answer: At 8-10% moisture in cool dry conditions: 12-18 months without significant quality loss (oil quality declines after 12 months). In hermetic bags: up to 24 months. In traditional jute bags: 6-12 months (depending on climate). In hot humid conditions: 3-6 months only. For seed purpose: use within 12 months for >80% germination.

question: How should mustard be dried before storage to prevent mold and fungal growth?
answer: 1) Sun drying: Spread on clean tarpaulin or cemented floor in thin layer (5-10 cm). 2) Turn every 2-3 hours for uniform drying. 3) Dry for 5-7 days (depending on sun). 4) Test moisture: Bite test (crisp) or moisture meter (target 8-10%). 5) Do not dry on bare soil (contamination). 6) For large scale: mechanical dryers (hot air 40-45°C). 7) Cool seeds before bagging.

question: What are the signs of spoilage or pest damage in stored mustard?
answer: Signs of spoilage: 1) Musty or sour smell (mold). 2) Clumping or caking (excess moisture). 3) Discolored seeds (dark brown black). 4) Sprouted seeds. 5) Heating (warm to touch). Pest damage: 1) Holes in seeds. 2) Fine dust/powder at bag bottom. 3) Webbing inside bag. 4) Live insects (weevils bruchids). 5) Empty seed hulls. Discard severely damaged seeds.

question: What food safety practices should be followed during mustard storage and handling?
answer: 1) Never use pesticide-treated seeds for oil extraction or consumption. 2) Do not store in containers that held chemicals/fertilizers. 3) Keep storage area clean and rodent-free. 4) Do not consume moldy seeds (may contain mycotoxins). 5) Wash hands after handling stored grain. 6) Use separate storage for seed vs. oilseed for consumption. 7) Follow PHI if field pesticides used. 8) For edible oil extraction use clean undamaged seeds.

question: How does frost (Quora) affect mustard and how can farmers protect it in Pakistan?
answer: Mustard is moderately frost tolerant at vegetative stage (down to -3°C). Frost at flowering (Jan-Feb in north) causes: 1) Flower drop (complete loss of that flush). 2) Damaged pods (empty or misshapen). 3) Stem cracking. Protection: 1) Sow at optimum time to avoid flowering during peak frost. 2) Irrigate before frost night (water releases heat). 3) Smoke: Burn moist crop residue upwind before dawn. 4) Use frost-tolerant varieties.

question: How does extreme heat (above 30°C) affect mustard production in Pakistan?
answer: Mustard is cool-season crop. Heat above 28°C: 1) Reduces germination (if at sowing). 2) Accelerates maturity (shorter duration). 3) Stops flowering and pod set (above 28°C). 4) Small shriveled seeds. 5) Reduced oil content (42% → 35%). 6) Increases pest pressure (aphids mites). Avoid late sowing (Dec) that pushes pod filling into March heat. In Sindh/South Punjab: sow by Nov 15 maximum.

question: How should a farmer manage mustard during unexpected heavy rainfall or flooding?
answer: 1) Immediately stop any irrigation. 2) Ensure drainage: Open channels to remove standing water. 3) If waterlogging <24 hours: plants may recover. 4) If >48 hours: root rot likely - assess survival. 5) After water recedes: apply light N (urea 15-20 kg/acre) for recovery. 6) Monitor for fungal diseases (white rust downy mildew) - prophylactic fungicide spray. 7) For flooded young crop: may need replanting if early season.

question: What is the effect of fog or cloud cover on mustard growth in winter in Pakistan?
answer: Prolonged fog (Dec-Jan in Punjab): 1) Reduces photosynthesis (low light). 2) Increases humidity (promotes white rust downy mildew). 3) Delays maturity. 4) Can cause etiolation (stretched weak stems). Management: 1) Wider row spacing (45 cm) for air circulation. 2) Preventive fungicide spray before fog period (Metalaxyl). 3) Avoid dense canopy (no excess N). 4) Use disease-resistant varieties (Raya Anmol).

question: How does hailstorm (Oola-bari) damage mustard and what can be done after hail?
answer: Hail damage: 1) Bruised stems (entry point for disease). 2) Shredded leaves. 3) Damaged pods (split). 4) Lodging (flattened crop). After hail: 1) Do not harvest immediately - wait 5-7 days for recovery assessment. 2) Apply fungicide (Mancozeb) to prevent infection through wounds. 3) Light N spray (1% urea) for recovery. 4) If >70% damage: consider alternative crop (if early season). 5) Report to agriculture department for possible compensation.

question: How should irrigation be adjusted for mustard during drought conditions in Pakistan?
answer: During drought: 1) Prioritize critical stages (flowering and pod fill) - irrigate these even if skip others. 2) Apply light irrigations (2-3 acre-inches) rather than heavy. 3) Use furrow irrigation (not flood) - more efficient. 4) Irrigate at night - less evaporation. 5) Mulch with crop residue (3-4 tons/acre) to conserve moisture. 6) If only 1 irrigation possible: apply at flowering (maximum yield response).

question: What climate-smart practices are recommended for mustard farmers in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Conservation agriculture: Zero-till/minimum till + residue retention (mulch). 2) Laser land leveling: Saves water improves uniformity. 3) Drought-tolerant varieties (P-18 Raya Anmol). 4) Weather-based sowing decisions (use advisory services). 5) Micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) where feasible (60% subsidy). 6) Agroforestry: Trees on field boundaries reduce wind speed. 7) Crop diversification: Mustard in rotation with climate-resilient crops (sorghum millet).

question: What is the impact of late monsoon or early monsoon on mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Mustard is Rabi crop (sown Oct-Nov) so monsoon (Jul-Sep) does not directly affect growing crop. However: Late monsoon (rains extending into Oct) delays land preparation and sowing - causes late sowing yield loss. Early monsoon (starting Mar) can damage mature crop (Feb-Mar harvest) causing pod splitting shattering and mold. Monitor forecasts and harvest promptly if early rains expected.

question: What government schemes or subsidies are available for mustard farmers in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Kisan Card: Subsidized fertilizer (Rs. 1000-2000/acre) and seeds. 2) Green Tractor Scheme: 50-70% subsidy on tractors (limited quota). 3) Solar Tube well subsidy: 60% for installation. 4) Drip/Sprinkler irrigation: 60-80% subsidy (PMKSY). 5) Soil testing: Free or Rs. 100/sample at govt labs. 6) Crop insurance: Premium subsidy (30-50%) under Kisan Package. 7) Oilseed promotion program (Ministry of Food Security) - subsidized mustard seed and fertilizer. Contact provincial agriculture department.

question: Which research institutes in Pakistan have developed improved mustard varieties?
answer: 1) Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI) Faisalabad - developed Raya Anmol. 2) National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC) Islamabad - developed P-18. 3) Barani Agricultural Research Institute (BARI) Chakwal - for rainfed varieties. 4) Oilseed Research Program NARC - general mustard improvement. 5) Sindh Agriculture University Tandojam - developed Sindh Raya. 6) Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC) - coordination.

question: Where can farmers in Pakistan get certified mustard seed?
answer: 1) Punjab Seed Corporation (PSC) - regional offices in Faisalabad Multan Lahore. 2) Provincial Agriculture Department extension centers. 3) Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad (direct sale). 4) NARC Islamabad (for P-18). 5) Barani Agricultural Research Chakwal (for rainfed varieties). 6) Progressive seed dealers (check certification tag). 7) Sindh Seed Corporation (for Sindh Raya). Price: Rs. 150-250/kg. Demand certified seed early (Aug-Oct) as limited quantity.

question: What extension services are available for mustard farmers in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Agriculture Department field staff (Agriculture Officers Field Assistants) - free advice. 2) Kisan Helpline 0800-15000 (Punjab) for queries. 3) SMS advisory services (CropMax Punjab) - weather pest alerts. 4) Farmer field schools (FFS) - hands-on training. 5) Agriculture extension WhatsApp groups (district level). 6) Mobile apps: "Agriculture Punjab" "Kisan Dost". 7) Radio/TV programs (Zaraat Nama on PBC). 8) Demonstration plots at union council level.

question: What loans or credit facilities are available for mustard cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: 1) ZTBL (Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited) - Production loans up to Rs. 50000/acre at markup 10-12%. 2) Bank of Punjab - Kisan Dost scheme. 3) National Bank of Pakistan - Agri loans. 4) Telenor Microfinance Bank (Easypaisa) - small loans. 5) Kisan Card (Punjab) - cash credit for inputs. Requirements: land ownership/lease record CNIC. Loan covers seed fertilizer pesticides. Repay after harvest.

question: What agricultural insurance is available for mustard crops in Pakistan?
answer: 1) PM Crop Insurance Scheme (under Kisan Package) - covers mustard (oilseeds). 2) Premium: 3-5% of sum insured (farmer pays 50% govt subsidy 50%). 3) Coverage: Yield loss >30% due to drought flood hail pests diseases. 4) Claim: Rs. 20000-50000/acre depending on coverage. 5) Providers: State Life Insurance Takaful Pakistan. Enrollment before sowing (Oct-Nov). Contact agriculture department for Kisan Card insurance component.

question: Where can a farmer in Pakistan report disease outbreaks or pest attacks on mustard?
answer: 1) District Agriculture Office (Extension) - immediate reporting. 2) Plant Protection Department - for locusts/quarantine pests. 3) Kisan Helpline 0800-15000 (Punjab). 4) Agriculture Complaint Cell 0800-30000. 5) Local Agriculture Field Assistant (FA) - village level. 6) WhatsApp groups of agriculture department. 7) Crop Reporting Centre (for statistics). For white rust or Alternaria outbreak: report early so advisory can be issued.

question: What role does the Provincial Agriculture Department play in supporting mustard farmers?
answer: 1) Provide extension services (field visits training). 2) Distribute subsidized inputs (seed fertilizer). 3) Soil testing facilities (free/low cost). 4) Pest/disease forecasting and alerts. 5) Subsidy administration (Kisan Card drip irrigation). 6) Organize farmer field days and demonstrations. 7) Link farmers with credit and insurance. 8) Research linkage (recommend improved varieties). 9) Market information and price updates. Contact Provincial Director Agriculture (extension wing).

question: What is onion and what is its agricultural importance in Pakistan?
answer: Onion (Allium cepa) known as Pyaz is an important rabi vegetable and cash crop in Pakistan. Its agricultural importance includes: 1) Essential vegetable in Pakistani cuisine (daily use). 2) High value cash crop (Rs. 100-200/kg in peak season). 3) Export potential to Middle East Central Asia and India. 4) Processing industry (dehydrated onion flakes onion powder pickles). 5) Medicinal properties (antioxidant anti-inflammatory). 6) Employment during planting and harvesting (40-50 laborers/acre). 7) Short duration (120-150 days) fits in multiple cropping systems.

question: What are the main growing regions of onion in Pakistan?
answer: Onion is grown throughout Pakistan. Major regions: Punjab: Vehari Khanewal Multan Sahiwal Okara Kasur Gujranwala Sialkot and Pothwar (Rawalpindi Attock). Sindh: Hyderabad Mirpurkhas Sanghar Nawabshah Badin Thatta. KPK: Peshawar Mardan Swabi Dera Ismail Khan Swat. Balochistan: Quetta Pishin Mastung Kalat Khuzdar (spring/summer crop).

question: What are the climate and temperature requirements for successful cultivation of onion in Pakistan?
answer: Onion requires cool to moderate climate. Optimum temperature: 13-24°C for vegetative growth 15-25°C for bulb formation. Minimum for germination: 10-12°C. Bulbing is triggered by day length (long day for northern varieties short day for southern). Bulbing temperature: 20-25°C. Frost damages seedlings. Dry weather at harvest essential. Requires 400-500mm rainfall or irrigation.

question: In which season(s) is onion cultivated in Pakistan (Rabi/Kharif)?
answer: Onion is grown in three seasons in Pakistan: 1) Rabi (winter) - main crop: sown October-November (nursery) transplanted December-January harvested March-May. 2) Kharif (summer) - sown March-April harvested July-September (Sindh South Punjab). 3) Spring - sown January-February harvested May-June (Balochistan KPK hills).

question: What is the typical crop duration/life cycle of onion from sowing to harvest?
answer: Typical crop duration is 120-160 days depending on variety and season. Early varieties: 100-120 days. Medium varieties: 120-140 days. Late varieties (storage): 140-160 days. Nursery phase: 40-50 days. Transplant to harvest: 80-120 days. In warm plains: shorter duration. In cool highlands: longer duration.

question: What are the growth stages of onion and what happens at each stage?
answer: 1) Nursery germination (0-15 days): Seed absorbs water radicle emerges. 2) Seedling (15-40 days): True leaves develop pencil-thick stage. 3) Transplanting (40-50 days): Seedlings moved to main field. 4) Vegetative growth (50-90 days): Leaf development root establishment. 5) Bulb initiation (90-100 days): Bulbing triggered by day length/temperature. 6) Bulb formation (100-130 days): Bulb swells leaves senesce. 7) Maturity (130-160 days): Tops fall over (neck softening) bulbs mature. 8) Harvest: When 50-70% tops have fallen.

question: How does onion contribute to food security and the farming economy in Pakistan?
answer: Onion contributes: 1) Essential daily vegetable for 220 million people. 2) Generates income for small farmers (Rs. 300000-800000/acre profit for hybrids). 3) Export earnings (fresh and dehydrated onion to UAE Sri Lanka Bangladesh Central Asia). 4) Employment during nursery transplanting weeding harvesting (50-60 laborers/acre). 5) Processing industry (onion powder flakes pickles). 6) Cold storage infrastructure supports off-season supply. 7) Buffer against price volatility (stored onion released during lean season).

question: How should land be prepared before transplanting onion in Pakistan?
answer: Land should be prepared to fine tilth (seedbed). Sequence: 1) Deep ploughing with disc plough (if hardpan). 2) 2-3 cultivations with cultivator. 3) Planking after each cultivation. 4) Laser leveling for uniform irrigation. 5) Raised bed formation (15-20 cm high 60-120 cm wide). 6) Final planking just before transplanting. For heavy soils: add 1-2 more cultivations.

question: How many ploughings are recommended for land preparation for onion?
answer: 5-7 ploughings/tillage passes: 1 deep ploughing (every 2-3 years) + 3-4 cultivator passes + 2 plankings. In heavy clay soils: 6-7 passes. In sandy soils: 4-5 passes. Fine seedbed is critical for small seedlings and bulb development.

question: What is the role of deep ploughing in onion cultivation?
answer: Deep ploughing (25-30 cm) with disc plough: 1) Breaks hardpan and improves root penetration. 2) Enhances water infiltration and drainage (critical for onion). 3) Exposes soil pests (cutworms nematodes) to predators. 4) Incorporates organic matter. 5) Reduces weed seed bank. Do once every 2-3 years.

question: What is the recommended land leveling (Laser Leveling) method before planting onion?
answer: Laser leveling is highly recommended. Benefits: 1) Uniform irrigation (prevents waterlogging in low spots - critical for onion). 2) Saves 20-30% irrigation water. 3) Improves transplant survival uniformity. 4) Reduces weed patches. Field leveled to ±1 cm variation. Service cost: Rs. 2000-3000/acre. Subsidy available.

question: Should ridges and furrows be made for onion cultivation in Pakistan? How?
answer: Raised beds (ridges and furrows) are essential for onion especially in heavy soils and rainy areas. Method: 1) Make raised beds 15-20 cm high 60-120 cm wide (2-4 rows per bed). 2) Furrow depth 15-20 cm. 3) Transplant onion seedlings on beds. Benefits: prevents waterlogging improves drainage reduces bulb rot and makes harvesting easier. Essential in clay soils.

question: How should previously harvested crop residue be managed before planting onion?
answer: 1) If previous crop was cereal (wheat rice maize): incorporate stubble by shallow ploughing. 2) Avoid planting onion after other Alliums (garlic leek) - minimum 3-4 year rotation. 3) Remove or deeply bury onion residues after harvest (disease carryover - Fusarium white rot). 4) For rice stubble: manage with disc harrow + cultivator. 5) Do not burn residue - incorporate for organic matter.

question: What pre-sowing irrigation (Raunni) is required for onion land preparation?
answer: Pre-sowing irrigation (raunni) given 15-20 days before transplanting when soil moisture is low. Apply 3-4 acre-inches water. After irrigation: allow soil to reach field capacity then cultivate when moisture at "good tilth". Saves 1-2 irrigations during crop growth. Essential for rainfed areas.

question: What implements and machinery are used for land preparation for onion in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Disc plough (deep ploughing). 2) Cultivator (3-4 passes). 3) Disc harrow (clod breaking). 4) Rotavator (fine seedbed - use moderately). 5) Plank (leveling and moisture conservation). 6) Laser land leveler. 7) Bed planter/ridger (for raised beds). 8) Rotary tiller (for seedbed).

question: How many days before transplanting should land preparation begin for onion?
answer: Start land preparation 15-20 days before transplanting. Timeline: Day 1: deep ploughing (if needed). Day 2-5: first cultivation + planking. Day 7-10: second cultivation + planking. Day 12-14: pre-transplant irrigation (if needed). Day 15-18: final cultivation + planking + bed making. Day 18-20: transplanting.

question: How does land preparation differ for irrigated vs. rainfed onion cultivation?
answer: Irrigated: finer seedbed required laser leveling important raised beds essential pre-transplant irrigation. Rainfed (Barani): focus on moisture conservation - fewer cultivations (4-5 passes) deep ploughing for water storage no pre-transplant irrigation rougher seedbed to reduce evaporation mulching. Rainfed onion not common - irrigation critical for bulb development.

question: What is the recommended seed rate for onion nursery in Pakistan?
answer: Seed rate: 6-8 kg per acre (for nursery covering 1 acre). For hybrid varieties: 4-5 kg/acre (seeds expensive). For open-pollinated varieties: 8-10 kg/acre. Nursery area: 1/10 to 1/8 acre (500-600 sq yards) for 1 acre main field. Use fresh high-germination seed (>80%).

question: What is the optimum row spacing and plant spacing for onion in Pakistan?
answer: Row spacing: 15-20 cm (6-8 inches) between rows. Plant to plant spacing: 10-15 cm (4-6 inches) after transplanting. On raised beds: 2-4 rows per bed (60-120 cm bed width). Target plant population: 200000-300000 plants per acre. Closer spacing for small bulbs (pickling) wider for large bulbs.

question: What is the recommended sowing depth for onion seeds in nursery?
answer: Nursery sowing depth: 1-2 cm (0.5-1 inch). In sandy soils: 2-2.5 cm. In heavy soils: 1-1.5 cm. Deeper than 3 cm reduces emergence. Shallower than 1 cm risks drying out. After sowing cover with fine soil or compost then light irrigation. Transplant seedlings at pencil thickness (40-50 days).

question: What sowing method is best for onion — broadcast (Chatha) drill dibbling or transplanting?
answer: Transplanting is the best and only method for onion in Pakistan. Steps: 1) Sow seeds in nursery bed. 2) Grow seedlings for 40-50 days. 3) Transplant to main field. Direct seeding is not practiced due to: poor emergence weed competition and difficulty in bulb formation. Broadcasting is used only in nursery. Dibbling is too labor intensive.

question: How should onion be transplanted after a previous crop (e.g. rice-wheat or cotton-wheat system)?
answer: 1) After rice: Allow field to dry (7-10 days). Prepare raised beds. Transplant onion Dec-Jan. 2) After cotton/wheat: Conventional tillage with 3-4 cultivations. 3) Ensure no herbicide carryover (pendimethalin from rice can damage onion - check labels). 4) In rice-wheat system onion can be planted after wheat harvest (spring crop in some areas). 5) Best rotation: maize - onion - wheat.

question: Can onion be transplanted using zero-till or minimum-till techniques in Pakistan?
answer: Zero-till transplanting is possible but not common. Method: 1) Prepare raised beds without deep ploughing (only surface tillage). 2) Transplant seedlings into beds. 3) Apply mulch. Benefits: saves 10-15 days and Rs. 2000-3000/acre land prep. Suitable for rice-onion system. Requires good drainage.

question: What equipment or tools are used for transplanting onion in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Manual transplanting (most common) - using hand or dibber (50-60 laborers/acre). 2) Onion transplanter (mechanical) - tractor-drawn or self-propelled (rare in Pakistan). 3) Dibber (wooden or metal) - for making holes. 4) String and markers (for row spacing). 5) Seedling trays (for hybrid onion - tray nursery).

question: What are all the major crop management activities for onion from sowing to harvest?
answer: Timeline: 0-50 days: nursery management (sowing irrigation weeding thinning pest control). 50-60 days: land preparation bed making transplanting. 60-90 days: vegetative growth - irrigation weeding (2-3 times) top dressing N (30 and 60 days) pest control (thrips). 90-120 days: bulb initiation and formation - irrigation disease control (purple blotch downy mildew). 120-150 days: bulb filling - reduce irrigation stop N. 150-160 days: stop irrigation harvest curing.

question: What is the complete activity calendar (timeline) for onion cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: October: nursery land preparation (1-15 Oct) nursery sowing (15-31 Oct). November: nursery management (irrigation weeding) (1-30 Nov). December: land preparation (1-15 Dec) transplanting (15-31 Dec). January: vegetative growth - irrigation first weeding first top dressing (1-31 Jan). February: second weeding second top dressing thrips control (1-28 Feb). March: bulb initiation - irrigation disease control (1-31 Mar). April: bulb filling - reduce irrigation stop N (1-30 Apr). May: stop irrigation (1-10 May) harvest (10-31 May) curing (15-31 May).

question: When should thinning be done in onion nursery and how?
answer: Thinning in nursery at 20-25 days after sowing when seedlings are 5-8 cm tall. Method: 1) Remove excess seedlings to achieve spacing 2-3 cm between plants. 2) Keep healthier vigorous seedlings. 3) Remove weak diseased and damaged seedlings. 4) Do not disturb roots of retained seedlings. 5) Irrigate lightly after thinning. Target: pencil-thick seedlings (40-50 days) for transplanting.

question: When should earthing up be done for onion and why?
answer: Earthing up (adding soil around plants) is generally not required for onion. For tall varieties or heavy soils: light earthing up at 40-50 days after transplanting. Method: pull soil slightly toward plant base (2-3 cm). Benefits: supports plants covers bulbs (prevents greening) improves drainage. Not practiced for most onion varieties.

question: How should inter-cultivation be done in onion fields?
answer: Inter-cultivation (weeding and soil loosening) at 20-25 days and 40-45 days after transplanting. Method: 1) Use hand hoe (khurpa) or wheel hoe. 2) Cultivate between rows at 2-3 cm depth (shallow - onion roots are shallow). 3) Avoid damaging bulbs. 4) Also breaks soil crust removes weeds aerates soil. For large areas: use power weeder (tractor-operated) with careful adjustment.

question: What is the process of transplanting onion seedlings and when should it be done?
answer: Transplanting process: 1) Prepare nursery 40-50 days before transplanting. 2) Water nursery 2-3 hours before pulling seedlings. 3) Gently pull seedlings (do not damage roots). 4) Sort seedlings - discard weak bolted or diseased ones. 5) Trim roots to 2-3 cm and leaves to 10-15 cm (optional - reduces transplant shock). 6) Transplant in main field at spacing 15x10 cm. 7) Plant at depth 2-3 cm (not too deep). 8) Irrigate immediately. Transplanting time: Rabi - Dec-Jan Kharif - April-May.

question: What is the optimal plant population per acre for onion in Pakistan?
answer: Optimal plant population: 200000-300000 plants per acre (50-75 plants per square meter). For large bulbs (export): 150000-200000 plants/acre. For medium bulbs (market): 250000-300000 plants/acre. For small bulbs (pickling): 350000-400000 plants/acre. Achieve by: spacing 15x10 cm gives approx 280000 plants/acre.
