answer: Purplish leaves delayed maturity poor fruit set.

question: What are the signs of potassium deficiency in tomato?
answer: Yellow leaf margins brown scorching small poor-quality fruits.

question: What are the signs of calcium deficiency in tomato?
answer: Blossom end rot (black sunken lesion on fruit bottom) on young fruits. Remedy: calcium nitrate foliar spray.

question: What happens if too much fertilizer (over-dose) is applied to tomato?
answer: Excess N: lush growth poor fruit set more disease (early blight). Excess K: can cause Mg deficiency. Excess fertilizer: salt injury leaf burn.

question: What are the recommended fertilizer products for tomato in Pakistan?
answer: Urea DAP SOP (potassium sulfate) Calcium nitrate SSP ZnSO4 Borax. Avoid MOP (chloride).

question: How should urea be applied to tomato to avoid losses?
answer: Apply just before irrigation. Incorporate into soil. Use neem-coated urea.

question: How many irrigations does tomato require in total?
answer: Tomato needs 10-15 irrigations depending on soil and season. Schedule: 1st immediately after transplanting then every 5-7 days in summer every 7-10 days in winter. Drip irrigation reduces frequency.

question: When should the first irrigation be given after transplanting?
answer: Immediately after transplanting (same day). Second at 5-7 days.

question: What are the critical growth stages for irrigation?
answer: Flowering (45-60 days) and fruit set (60-75 days) are critical. Water stress at flowering causes flower drop (30-50% loss). Stress at fruit set causes small fruits and cracking.

question: How many days apart should irrigations be given in summer?
answer: Summer tomato (highlands): interval 5-7 days.

question: How many days apart should irrigations be given in winter?
answer: Winter tomato (main crop): interval 7-12 days.

question: What is the total water requirement of tomato?
answer: 400-600 acre-inches (10-15 million liters per acre).

question: What irrigation method is suitable for tomato?
answer: Drip irrigation is best (saves 40-50% water reduces disease). Furrow irrigation also good. Avoid overhead irrigation (promotes late blight).

question: How does drip irrigation improve tomato production?
answer: Saves water allows fertigation keeps foliage dry (reduces blight) reduces fruit cracking increases yield 20-30%.

question: What are the signs of water stress in tomato?
answer: Wilting flower drop fruit cracking small fruits blossom end rot (calcium uptake affected).

question: What are the signs of waterlogging in tomato?
answer: Yellow leaves root rot plant death. Drain immediately.

question: Should tomato irrigation be stopped before harvest?
answer: No - maintain uniform moisture. Fluctuations cause fruit cracking. Reduce irrigation slightly as fruits ripen.

question: How does canal water vs. tube well (brackish) water affect tomato?
answer: Canal water best. Brackish water (EC >1.5) causes leaf burn reduced yield. If only saline: mix with canal water apply gypsum.

question: What is the average yield of tomato per acre in Pakistan?
answer: Average: 150-200 maunds/acre (6000-8000 kg) for open-pollinated. Hybrid: 300-500 maunds/acre. Tunnel: 500-800 maunds/acre.

question: What is the maximum achievable yield?
answer: 800-1000 maunds/acre (32000-40000 kg) in tunnel with hybrid varieties.

question: What are the main reasons for low yield?
answer: Fruit borer (20-40% loss) late blight (30-50% loss) TLCV (50-80% loss) poor pollination (flower drop) nutrient imbalance.

question: How can a farmer increase yield?
answer: Use hybrid seed staking and pruning drip irrigation balanced NPK + Ca pest/disease control.

question: What are high-yielding varieties?
answer: Sahel (hybrid) 400-500 maunds T-1359 300-400 maunds Nageeb 300-350 maunds.

question: What are the top 5 things to double yield?
answer: 1) Hybrid seed. 2) Staking + pruning. 3) Drip irrigation + fertigation. 4) Fruit borer and late blight control. 5) Calcium and boron application.

question: When is tomato ready for harvest?
answer: Harvest when fruits reach full color (red pink yellow) but still firm. For local market: 75-90% color. For long distance: 30-50% color (breaker stage).

question: What are the visual signs of maturity?
answer: Fruit color changes from green to red/orange. Firmness (slight give). Easy separation from calyx.

question: How is tomato harvested?
answer: Manual picking. Twist and pull fruits with calyx attached. Handle gently. Pick every 3-5 days. Harvest in morning.

question: What is the correct harvesting time in Punjab?
answer: Spring crop: April-May. Autumn crop: January-March. Tunnel: December-March.

question: How long after transplanting is tomato harvested?
answer: 45-60 days after transplanting for first pick. Harvest continues for 30-60 days.

question: How should tomato be stored after harvest?
answer: Store at 12-15°C (not below 10°C - chilling injury). Humidity 85-90%. Shelf life 7-14 days. Do not store with ethylene-producing fruits.

question: What is the ideal temperature for tomato storage?
answer: Green tomatoes: 12-15°C. Ripe tomatoes: 8-10°C. Below 10°C causes chilling injury (watery texture).

question: What are major post-harvest losses?
answer: Bruising (10-20%) rot (5-15%) over-ripening. Reduce by careful handling grading cold storage.

question: How does frost affect tomato?
answer: Frost kills plants. Transplant after frost risk (Feb in plains). In tunnels use heaters.

question: How does extreme heat (above 35°C) affect tomato?
answer: Flower drop poor fruit set small fruits. Use heat-tolerant varieties (Salar). Shade net in summer.

question: How does hail damage tomato?
answer: Shreds leaves bruises fruits. After hail apply fungicide (Mancozeb).

question: What government schemes are available for tomato farmers?
answer: Kisan Card (fertilizer subsidy) Green Tractor Scheme drip irrigation subsidy (60-80%) crop insurance.

question: Which institutes developed tomato varieties?
answer: Ayub Research (T-1359) Vegetable Research Institute Sahiwal (Nageeb) NARC (Salar).

question: Where to get certified tomato seed?
answer: Punjab Seed Corporation Agriculture Extension private seed companies (Syngenta Nunhems Seminis).

question: What extension services are available?
answer: Kisan Helpline 0800-15000 SMS alerts farmer field schools mobile apps.

question: What loans are available for tomato?
answer: ZTBL Bank of Punjab (Kisan Dost) Kisan Card.

question: What agricultural insurance is available for tomato?
answer: PM Crop Insurance Scheme covers tomato. Premium subsidy 50%.

question: Where to report tomato disease outbreaks?
answer: District Agriculture Office Kisan Helpline local Field Assistant.

question: What is turnip and what is its agricultural importance in Pakistan?
answer: Turnip (Brassica rapa) known as Shaljam is an important rabi vegetable and fodder crop in Pakistan. Its agricultural importance includes: 1) Edible root consumed raw in salads or cooked in curries. 2) Leaves (saag) used as green vegetable. 3) High-value cash crop for winter markets (Rs. 40-80/kg). 4) Short duration (50-70 days) fits in multiple cropping systems. 5) Excellent fodder for livestock (roots and leaves). 6) Can be grown on marginal soils. 7) Pickling and processing potential.

question: What are the main growing regions of turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Turnip is grown throughout Pakistan. Major regions: Punjab: Lahore Kasur Okara Sahiwal Multan Faisalabad Gujranwala Sialkot Rawalpindi Attock Chakwal. Sindh: Hyderabad Mirpurkhas Sukkur Larkana. KPK: Peshawar Mardan Swabi Mansehra Abbottabad Dera Ismail Khan. Balochistan: Quetta Pishin Mastung Kalat (spring/summer crop). Grown in both plains and hills.

question: What are the climate and temperature requirements for successful cultivation of turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Turnip requires cool temperate climate. Optimum temperature: 10-18°C for root development. Minimum germination: 5-7°C. High temperature (>25°C) causes pithiness (hollow roots) and pungency. Frost improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar). Needs 300-400mm rainfall or irrigation. Long days promote bolting short days favor root growth.

question: In which season(s) is turnip cultivated in Pakistan (Rabi/Kharif)?
answer: Turnip is primarily a Rabi (winter) crop in plains: sown September-November harvested October-February. In high altitude areas (Balochistan KPK hills) it is grown as spring/summer crop: sown March-April harvested June-July. Also autumn crop in August-September.

question: What is the typical crop duration/life cycle of turnip from sowing to harvest?
answer: Typical crop duration is 50-80 days depending on variety. Early varieties: 45-55 days. Medium: 55-70 days. Late (fodder/storage): 70-90 days. In warm conditions: shorter duration (45-55 days). In cool conditions: longer (60-80 days).

question: What are the growth stages of turnip and what happens at each stage?
answer: 1) Germination (0-8 days): Seed absorbs water radicle emerges. 2) Seedling (8-20 days): First true leaves taproot begins to swell. 3) Root enlargement (20-50 days): Hypocotyl thickens rapidly (edible root forms). 4) Maturity (50-80 days): Root reaches marketable size (5-10 cm diameter). 5) Bolting (if delayed): Flower stalk emerges root becomes pithy (not marketable).

question: How does turnip contribute to food security and the farming economy in Pakistan?
answer: Turnip contributes: 1) Affordable winter vegetable for daily consumption. 2) Quick returns (50-70 days) - ideal for catch cropping after rice. 3) Generates income for small farmers (Rs. 150000-250000/acre profit). 4) Leaves as nutritious fodder for livestock (reduces feed cost). 5) Can be stored for 2-3 months in winter. 6) Fits in rice-wheat system as a short-duration crop.

question: How should land be prepared before sowing turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Land prepared to fine tilth. Sequence: 1) Deep ploughing. 2) 2-3 cultivations. 3) Planking. 4) Laser leveling. 5) Raised bed formation (10-15 cm high 60-120 cm wide). 6) Final planking.

question: How many ploughings are recommended for land preparation for turnip?
answer: 4-6 ploughings: 1 deep ploughing + 2-3 cultivator passes + 2 plankings. In heavy clay: 5-6 passes.

question: What is the role of deep ploughing in turnip cultivation?
answer: Deep ploughing (20-25 cm): 1) Breaks hardpan for root penetration. 2) Enhances drainage. 3) Exposes soil pests. 4) Incorporates organic matter.

question: What is the recommended land leveling (Laser Leveling) method before planting turnip?
answer: Laser leveling recommended for uniform irrigation and drainage. Saves water 20-30%.

question: Should ridges and furrows be made for turnip cultivation in Pakistan? How?
answer: Raised beds (ridges and furrows) recommended for heavy soils. Method: Make beds 10-15 cm high 60-120 cm wide (2-4 rows per bed). Furrow depth 10-15 cm. Benefits: drainage root shape easy harvest.

question: How should previously harvested crop residue be managed before planting turnip?
answer: Incorporate previous crop residues (wheat rice maize). Avoid planting turnip after other brassicas - minimum 3-year rotation.

question: What pre-sowing irrigation (Raunni) is required for turnip land preparation?
answer: Pre-sowing irrigation given 10-15 days before sowing if soil dry. Apply 2-3 acre-inches.

question: What implements and machinery are used for land preparation for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Disc plough cultivator rotavator plank laser land leveler bed planter/ridger.

question: How many days before sowing should land preparation begin for turnip?
answer: Start 10-15 days before sowing. Day 1-5: ploughing. Day 5-10: cultivation bed making.

question: How does land preparation differ for irrigated vs. rainfed turnip cultivation?
answer: Rainfed turnip is limited. Irrigated: finer seedbed laser leveling raised beds. Rainfed: moisture conservation deeper ploughing rougher seedbed mulching.

question: What is the recommended seed rate (kg/acre) for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Seed rate: 3-4 kg per acre for direct sowing. For small-seeded varieties: 2.5-3 kg. For bold-seeded: 4-5 kg. Use fresh high-germination seed (>80%).

question: What is the optimum row spacing and plant spacing for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Row spacing: 30-45 cm. Plant to plant spacing: 8-12 cm after thinning. On raised beds: 2-4 rows per bed. Target population: 200000-300000 plants per acre.

question: What is the recommended sowing depth for turnip seeds in Pakistan?
answer: Sowing depth: 1.5-2.5 cm. In sandy soils: 2.5-3 cm. In heavy soils: 1-1.5 cm. Deeper than 3 cm reduces emergence.

question: What sowing method is best for turnip — broadcast (Chatha) drill dibbling or transplanting?
answer: Drill sowing is best for uniform spacing. Broadcasting is common but leads to overcrowding. Transplanting NOT practiced for turnip (taproot sensitive).

question: How should turnip be sown after a previous crop (e.g. rice-wheat system)?
answer: After rice: allow field to dry 7-10 days sow turnip Sep-Oct. After wheat: sow as spring crop (Jan-Feb). Best rotation: maize - turnip - wheat.

question: Can turnip be sown using zero-till or minimum-till techniques in Pakistan?
answer: Zero-till possible. Sow directly into standing stubble (after rice). Use zero-till drill. Benefits: saves time moisture conservation.

question: What equipment or tools are used for sowing turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Seed drill manual dibber string for row marking. Broadcasting by hand common.

question: What are the major crop management activities for turnip?
answer: Land prep sowing thinning (10-15 days) weeding (2 times) irrigation fertilization pest control harvest.

question: When should thinning (Gidai) be done in turnip?
answer: Thinning at 10-15 days after sowing when plants 5-8 cm tall. Remove excess plants to achieve spacing 8-12 cm.

question: How should inter-cultivation be done in turnip fields?
answer: Weeding at 15-20 days and 30-35 days. Shallow cultivation (2-3 cm) to avoid root damage.

question: What is the optimal plant population per acre for turnip?
answer: 200000-300000 plants per acre (spacing 30-45 cm row × 8-12 cm plant).

question: What are the most commonly grown varieties of turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Commonly grown varieties include: 1) Purple Top White Globe (purple shoulder white bottom) - most popular. 2) Golden Ball (yellow flesh). 3) Early White (white all over). 4) Desi Shaljam (local small round). 5) Peshawar Local (adapted to cooler areas). 6) Snowball (cold tolerant). 7) Forage turnip (large roots for livestock). Traditional varieties yield 150-250 maunds/acre.

question: What are the improved and recommended varieties of turnip approved by Pakistani agricultural research institutes?
answer: Improved varieties approved by PARC/NARC/Ayub Research: 1) Purple Top White Globe (Vegetable Research Institute Sahiwal) - purple shoulder white flesh yield 200-300 maunds/acre excellent storage. 2) Golden Ball (Ayub Research Faisalabad) - yellow flesh high sugar content. 3) Early White (NARC) - early maturing 50-55 days. 4) Snowball (for northern areas) - frost tolerant. 5) Forage Turnip (Ayub Research) - high biomass for livestock.

question: What are the early-maturing medium-maturing and late-maturing varieties of turnip available in Pakistan?
answer: Early-maturing (45-55 days): Early White Desi Local. Medium-maturing (55-70 days): Purple Top White Globe Snowball. Late-maturing (70-90 days): Golden Ball Forage Turnip. Early varieties for early market (higher price). Late varieties for storage and livestock.

question: What are high-yielding varieties of turnip?
answer: Purple Top White Globe (250-300 maunds) Golden Ball (200-250).

question: What type of soil is best suited for growing turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Well-drained sandy loam or loamy soil rich in organic matter is best. Deep loose soil (30-45 cm) allows round root development. Avoid heavy clays (roots become misshapen forked) and very sandy soils (low water holding). pH 6.0-7.0.

question: What is the ideal soil pH range for turnip cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Ideal pH range is 6.0 to 7.0 (slightly acidic to neutral). Turnip can tolerate pH 5.5-7.5 but roots become pungent and misshapen below 5.5. At high pH >7.0: clubroot disease risk increases.

question: What soil texture (loamy sandy clayey) is most suitable for turnip?
answer: Sandy loam and loam are most suitable - provide good drainage aeration and easy root expansion. Sandy soils: produce smaller roots but good for early crop. Clayey soils: problematic - roots become forked hairy misshapen and difficult to harvest.

question: Can turnip be grown on saline or sodic soils (Kallar) in Pakistan? What are the precautions?
answer: Turnip is moderately salt-sensitive (ECe <3 dS/m). Not recommended on saline soils. If unavoidable: 1) Apply gypsum. 2) Heavy leaching. 3) Use raised beds. 4) Add FYM 15-20 tons/acre. 5) Use salt-tolerant varieties (limited).

question: What soil drainage conditions are required for turnip?
answer: Good drainage is essential. Turnip is sensitive to waterlogging - standing water causes root rot and splitting. Raised beds (10-15 cm high) recommended in heavy soils.

question: How does soil organic matter content affect the yield of turnip?
answer: Higher organic matter (2-3%) improves: 1) Root size and uniformity (no forking). 2) Water holding capacity. 3) Nutrient availability. 4) Flavor (sweet not pungent). Every 0.5% increase in OM boosts yield by 5-10 maunds/acre.

question: What soil testing should a farmer do before planting turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Essential tests: pH EC organic matter available N P K Boron (B) - prevents hollow roots. Sample depth 6-9 inches.

question: How should soil fertility be maintained or improved for repeated cultivation of turnip?
answer: 1) Crop rotation: turnip after cereals (wheat maize) - not after other brassicas (cabbage cauliflower radish) to avoid clubroot. 2) Apply FYM 8-10 tons/acre every 2-3 years. 3) Green manuring. 4) Balanced NPK fertilization.

question: What are the signs of poor or unsuitable soil for turnip cultivation?
answer: Signs: 1) Water pooling (poor drainage). 2) White salt crust. 3) Forked hairy misshapen roots (clay or compacted soil). 4) Hollow pithy roots (boron deficiency or heat). 5) Stunted plants (N deficiency).

question: What soil preparation practices improve the structure and health of soil for turnip?
answer: 1) Deep ploughing (20-25 cm). 2) Add organic matter (FYM). 3) Green manuring. 4) Gypsum for sodic soils. 5) Laser leveling. 6) Raised bed preparation (10-15 cm high).

question: When is the best time to sow turnip in Punjab Pakistan?
answer: Optimum sowing: Rabi: September 15 to November 15. Central Punjab: Oct 1-Nov 15. South Punjab: Sep 15-Oct 31. Spring: January 15-February 28. Summer (highlands): March-April.

question: When is the best time to sow turnip in Sindh Pakistan?
answer: Sindh: September 15 to November 30. Lower Sindh: Oct 1-Nov 30. Upper Sindh: Sep 15-Oct 31. Spring: January 1-February 15.

question: When is the best time to sow turnip in KPK Pakistan?
answer: KPK: September 1 to October 31. Peshawar valley: Sep 15-Oct 31. Spring: February-March. Summer (high elevations): March-April.

question: When is the best time to sow turnip in Balochistan Pakistan?
answer: Balochistan: Spring crop: February 15 to April 15. Quetta/Pishin: Mar 1-Apr 15. Summer (high valleys): April-May. Autumn (plains): September-October.

question: When is the best time to sow turnip in South Punjab (Multan Bahawalpur DG Khan)?
answer: South Punjab: Autumn: September 15 to October 31. Spring: January 15-February 15.

question: What happens if turnip is sown too early or too late in Pakistan?
answer: Too early (August): high temperatures cause pithiness (hollow roots) bolting pungent bitter roots. Too late (December): slow growth (cold) small roots lower yield (30-50% loss).

question: How does sowing time affect the yield and quality of turnip?
answer: Each week delay after Oct 15 reduces yield 5-10%. Optimum Oct sowing gives 200-300 maunds/acre. Quality: late sowing produces small roots early sowing causes pithiness and bolting.

question: What seed treatment (Zahar-alood) should be done before sowing turnip seeds?
answer: Seed treatment recommended: 1) Fungicide for seed-borne diseases (Alternaria). 2) Insecticide for early pests. Treat seeds 24 hours before sowing.

question: Which fungicide is recommended for seed treatment of turnip?
answer: Carbendazim 2g per kg seed. Thiram 2.5g per kg seed. Metalaxyl 2g per kg - effective against downy mildew.

question: Which insecticide is recommended for seed treatment of turnip?
answer: Imidacloprid 5ml per kg seed - controls early aphids and flea beetles. Chlorpyrifos 2-3ml per kg for cutworms.

question: What is the process of seed treatment for turnip?
answer: Mix fungicide + insecticide in 30-50ml water per kg seed. Spread seeds on polythene. Pour solution while mixing. Dry in shade. Sow within 24-48 hours.

question: Should turnip seeds be soaked in water before sowing?
answer: No. Soaking causes clumping and rot. Dry seed treatment is best.

question: How does seed treatment affect germination rate?
answer: Increases germination from 70-80% to 90-95% and protects from damping off.

question: What is bio-priming for turnip seeds?
answer: Treat seeds with Trichoderma harzianum 5g per kg seed or Pseudomonas fluorescens for bio-control.

question: How should treated turnip seed be stored before sowing?
answer: Sow within 24-48 hours. Do not store more than 7 days.

question: What are safety precautions for seed treatment?
answer: Wear gloves and mask. Avoid inhalation. Wash hands after.

question: What are the major weeds in turnip fields?
answer: Bathu Maina Peeli Buti wild oat Cyperus rotundus Cynodon dactylon.

question: What is the critical period of weed competition?
answer: 10-35 days after sowing. Weeds cause 50-70% yield loss.

question: What herbicides are recommended for turnip?
answer: Pre-emergence: Pendimethalin 500-600ml/acre. Post-emergence: Quizalofop for grasses. Manual weeding for broadleaf.

question: How many manual weedings are recommended?
answer: 2 manual weedings at 15-20 days and 30-35 days.

question: What are the major insect pests of turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Flea beetle (Phyllotreta) - most damaging on seedlings. Aphids (Lipaphis erysimi). Cutworms. Cabbage white butterfly (caterpillar). Leaf miner.

question: How to identify flea beetle damage?
answer: Small round holes (shot holes) on leaves. Severe: skeletonized leaves. Seedlings can be killed.

question: How to control flea beetle?
answer: Imidacloprid 250ml/acre. Carbaryl 400g/acre. For organic: neem oil.

question: What are the major diseases of turnip?
answer: Alternaria leaf spot (black spots). Downy mildew (yellow patches with fuzz). Clubroot (swollen distorted roots) - soil-borne. White rust.

question: How to identify clubroot?
answer: Roots become swollen distorted (clubs). Plants stunted yellow. Soil-borne fungus persists 10+ years.

question: How to control clubroot?
answer: No cure. Crop rotation (7-10 years). Lime to raise pH above 7.2. Resistant varieties (limited).

question: How to identify Alternaria leaf spot?
answer: Small dark brown spots with concentric rings on leaves. Yellow halo.

question: How to control Alternaria?
answer: Mancozeb 500g/acre. Chlorothalonil. Crop rotation.

question: What are the recommended fertilizers for turnip cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Turnip requires: Nitrogen (leaf growth) Phosphorus (root development) Potassium (root quality). Use Urea DAP SOP. Boron prevents hollow roots. FYM 8-10 tons/acre.

question: What is the recommended NPK dose per acre for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: NPK: 30-40 kg N + 40-50 kg P2O5 + 40-50 kg K2O per acre. For low fertility: N=40 P=50 K=50. Boron: 1-2 kg/acre (borax).

question: What is the recommended dose of nitrogen (N) fertilizer for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: 30-40 kg N per acre. Apply in 2 splits: 1/2 at sowing 1/2 at 20-25 days (root enlargement). Excess N causes pithiness.

question: What is the recommended dose of phosphorus (P) fertilizer for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: 40-50 kg P2O5 per acre. Apply full dose at sowing (basal).

question: What is the recommended dose of potassium (K) fertilizer for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: 40-50 kg K2O per acre. Apply full dose at sowing. Potassium improves root size sweetness and storage.

question: When and how should the first dose of fertilizer (Basal Dose) be applied to turnip?
answer: Basal: full P and K + 1/2 N applied at sowing. Broadcast and incorporate into soil.

question: When and how should the second and subsequent doses (Top Dressing) be applied to turnip?
answer: Top dressing: remaining 1/2 N at 20-25 days after sowing. Broadcast between rows before irrigation.

question: What is the role of boron (B) fertilizer in turnip cultivation?
answer: Boron prevents hollow root (pithiness) and internal browning. Deficiency causes cracked roots. Apply borax 1-2 kg/acre at sowing. Foliar spray 0.1% boric acid at 20 days.

question: What micronutrient deficiencies are commonly observed in turnip in Pakistani soils?
answer: Boron (B) - hollow roots cracking. Zinc (Zn) - stunted growth. Iron (Fe) - interveinal chlorosis in high pH soils.

question: How can organic fertilizers (FYM compost) be used for turnip?
answer: Apply FYM 8-10 tons/acre 15-20 days before sowing. Improves root quality and soil structure.

question: What is the recommended dose of farmyard manure (FYM) for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: 8-10 tons (160-200 maunds) per acre. Well-rotted FYM.

question: How does fertilizer application differ for irrigated vs. rainfed turnip cultivation?
answer: Rainfed turnip limited. Irrigated: split N. Rainfed: all fertilizer at sowing lower N (25-30 kg/acre).

question: What are the signs of nitrogen deficiency in turnip?
answer: Pale green leaves stunted growth small roots. Remedy: apply urea 10-15 kg/acre.

question: What are the signs of phosphorus deficiency in turnip?
answer: Purplish leaves delayed maturity poor root development.

question: What are the signs of potassium deficiency in turnip?
answer: Yellow leaf margins small roots poor storage quality.

question: What are the signs of boron deficiency in turnip?
answer: Hollow pithy roots cracking internal browning. Remedy: borax application.

question: What happens if too much fertilizer (over-dose) is applied to turnip?
answer: Excess N: lush leaves hollow roots poor quality. Excess fertilizer: salt injury leaf burn.

question: What are the recommended fertilizer products for turnip in Pakistan?
answer: Urea DAP SOP SSP borax ZnSO4.

question: How should urea be applied to turnip to avoid losses?
answer: Apply before irrigation. Incorporate into soil. Use neem-coated urea.

question: How many irrigations does turnip require in total?
answer: Turnip needs 6-10 irrigations. Schedule: 1st immediately after sowing then every 7-10 days. Stop 5-7 days before harvest.

question: When should the first irrigation be given after sowing?
answer: Immediately after sowing (same day). Second at 5-7 days.

question: What are the critical growth stages for irrigation?
answer: Root enlargement (20-40 days) is critical. Water stress causes small pithy pungent roots (30-50% loss).

question: How many days apart should irrigations be given in winter?
answer: Winter: interval 7-12 days. Sandy soils: 5-7 days. Loamy: 7-10 days. Clay: 10-12 days.

question: What is the total water requirement of turnip?
answer: 300-500 acre-inches (7-12 million liters per acre).

question: What irrigation method is suitable for turnip?
answer: Furrow irrigation best. Drip excellent (saves water reduces leaf disease). Avoid overhead irrigation (promotes downy mildew).

question: How does drip irrigation improve turnip production?
answer: Saves 40-50% water keeps foliage dry reduces disease increases yield 20-30%.

question: What are the signs of water stress in turnip?
answer: Wilting leaves small pithy roots pungent taste premature bolting.

question: What are the signs of waterlogging in turnip?
answer: Yellow leaves root rot splitting. Drain immediately.

question: Should turnip irrigation be stopped before harvest?
answer: Yes stop 5-7 days before harvest to improve root firmness and sweetness.

question: How does canal water vs. tube well (brackish) water affect turnip?
answer: Canal water best. Brackish water (EC >1.5) damages turnip. Avoid.

question: What is the average yield of turnip per acre in Pakistan?
answer: Average: 150-200 maunds/acre (6000-8000 kg). Progressive: 250-300 maunds.

question: What is the maximum achievable yield?
answer: 350-400 maunds/acre (14000-16000 kg) with improved variety and drip irrigation.

question: What are the main reasons for low yield?
answer: Flea beetle damage (20-40% loss) clubroot (50% loss) pithiness from heat late sowing poor soil.

question: How can a farmer increase yield?
answer: Use Purple Top White Globe variety boron application flea beetle control timely sowing (Oct).

question: What are the top 5 things to double yield?
answer: 1) Improved variety (Purple Top). 2) Boron application (prevents hollow). 3) Flea beetle control. 4) Timely sowing (Oct). 5) Raised beds + drip irrigation.

question: What diseases affect turnip?
answer: Alternaria leaf spot (black spots). Downy mildew (yellow patches with fuzz). Clubroot (swollen distorted roots) - soil-borne. White rust.

question: When is turnip ready for harvest?
answer: 50-80 days after sowing when roots reach 5-10 cm diameter. Harvest when roots are firm smooth not pithy.

question: What are the visual signs of maturity?
answer: Root shoulder visible above soil. Size appropriate for variety. Leaves still green but not overgrown.

question: How is turnip harvested?
answer: Manual: loosen soil with khurpa/spade then pull by leaves. Remove leaves (leave 1-2 cm stem). Grade by size.

question: What is the correct harvesting time in Punjab?
answer: Autumn crop: October-December. Spring crop: March-April.

question: How long after sowing is turnip harvested?
answer: 45-80 days depending on variety.

question: How should turnip be stored after harvest?
answer: Remove leaves. Store in cool dark place (0-5°C 90-95% RH) in perforated bags. Lasts 2-3 months.

question: What is the ideal temperature for turnip storage?
answer: 0-2°C for long-term storage (2-3 months). High humidity (90-95%) prevents shriveling.

question: What are major post-harvest losses?
answer: Shriveling (10-20%) rot (5-15%) pithiness (if harvested late). Reduce by proper storage.

question: How does frost affect turnip?
answer: Frost improves sweetness (converts starch to sugar). Heavy frost (-5°C) damages roots. Mulch for protection.

question: How does extreme heat (above 25°C) affect turnip?
answer: Causes pithiness (hollow roots) pungency bolting. Avoid summer sowing in plains.

question: What are heat-tolerant turnip varieties?
answer: Early White - short duration escapes heat. Not recommended for summer in plains.

question: How should irrigation be adjusted during drought?
answer: Prioritize root enlargement stage (20-40 days). Drip irrigation most efficient.

question: What government schemes are available for turnip farmers?
answer: Kisan Card drip irrigation subsidy (60-80%) crop insurance.

question: Which institutes developed turnip varieties?
answer: Ayub Research (Golden Ball) Vegetable Research Institute Sahiwal (Purple Top White Globe) NARC (Early White).

question: Where to get certified turnip seed?
answer: Punjab Seed Corporation Agriculture Extension progressive dealers.

question: What extension services are available?
answer: Kisan Helpline SMS alerts farmer field schools.

question: What loans are available for turnip?
answer: ZTBL Bank of Punjab (Kisan Dost) Kisan Card.

question: What agricultural insurance is available for turnip?
answer: PM Crop Insurance Scheme covers turnip. Premium subsidy 50%.

question: Where to report turnip disease outbreaks?
answer: District Agriculture Office Kisan Helpline local Field Assistant.

question: What role does the Provincial Agriculture Department play?
answer: Extension services subsidized inputs soil testing pest forecasting subsidy administration.

question: What is wheat and what is its agricultural importance in Pakistan?
answer: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) known as Gandum is the staple food crop and the most important cereal in Pakistan. Its agricultural importance includes: 1) Primary source of calories (60-70% of daily diet) for 220 million people. 2) Covers the largest area of any crop (over 9 million hectares). 3) Provides employment for millions of farmers and laborers. 4) Government procurement and price support system ensures food security. 5) Wheat straw is valuable livestock feed. 6) Contributes 1.5-2% to national GDP. 7) Foundation of the rice-wheat cropping system that feeds South Asia.

question: What are the main growing regions of wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Wheat is grown in all provinces but major regions: Punjab: entire province especially central Punjab (Faisalabad Sahiwal Okara Sargodha) south Punjab (Multan Bahawalpur Rahim Yar Khan) and north Punjab (Rawalpindi Attock Chakwal). Sindh: Sukkur Jacobabad Larkana Hyderabad Mirpurkhas. KPK: Peshawar Mardan Dera Ismail Khan Swabi. Balochistan: Nasirabad Jaffarabad Quetta valley. Rainfed (Barani) areas: Pothwar plateau.

question: What are the climate and temperature requirements for successful cultivation of wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Wheat requires cool temperate climate. Optimum temperature: 20-25°C for germination 15-20°C for tillering 20-25°C for grain filling. Minimum temperature for growth: 4-5°C. Maximum tolerance: 35°C (above this causes forced maturity and shriveled grain). Frost at flowering (>-2°C) damages flowers. Needs 300-400mm rainfall or equivalent irrigation. Dry weather at harvest essential.

question: In which season(s) is wheat cultivated in Pakistan (Rabi/Kharif)?
answer: Wheat is exclusively a Rabi (winter) crop in Pakistan. Sown from October to December and harvested from March to May. In high altitude areas of Balochistan and KPK it can be sown as late as December-January (spring wheat) but yields are lower.

question: What is the typical crop duration/life cycle of wheat from sowing to harvest?
answer: Typical crop duration is 130-160 days depending on variety and climate. Early varieties: 130-140 days. Medium: 140-150 days. Late: 150-160 days. In warm plains (Sindh): shorter duration (120-135 days). In cooler areas (Pothwar): longer (150-165 days).

question: What are the growth stages of wheat and what happens at each stage?
answer: 1) Germination (0-10 days): Seed absorbs water radicle and shoot emerge. 2) Seedling (10-25 days): First leaves develop root system establishes. 3) Tillering (25-45 days): Secondary shoots (tillers) form - determines number of grain heads. 4) Stem elongation (45-60 days): Internodes lengthen flag leaf emerges. 5) Booting (60-70 days): Head swells in leaf sheath. 6) Heading (70-80 days): Head emerges from flag leaf. 7) Flowering (80-90 days): Anthesis occurs - critical for grain set. 8) Grain filling (90-120 days): Kernels fill and harden. 9) Maturity (120-160 days): Plants turn golden brown grain hard.

question: How does wheat contribute to food security and the farming economy in Pakistan?
answer: Wheat is the foundation of Pakistan's food security. It provides: 1) Daily bread (roti) for 220 million people. 2) Employment for millions of farmers and laborers. 3) Government procurement (over 8 million tons annually) stabilizes prices. 4) Wheat straw is essential livestock feed. 5) Export surplus in good years earns foreign exchange. 6) Supports flour milling industry (over 2000 mills). 7) The rice-wheat system is the backbone of Punjab agriculture.

question: How should land be prepared before sowing wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Land should be prepared to fine tilth but not over-pulverized. Sequence: After rice: 1-2 disc harrowings + 2 cultivations + planking. After cotton: 2-3 cultivations + planking. After fallow: 3 cultivations + 2 plankings. Laser leveling for uniform moisture. For zero-till: direct drilling without cultivation.

question: How many ploughings are recommended for land preparation for wheat?
answer: 3-5 ploughings/tillage passes depending on previous crop. After rice: 3-4 passes. After cotton: 2-3 passes. After fallow: 4-5 passes. In heavy clay soils: 4-5 passes. In sandy soils: 2-3 passes. Each pass should be at different angles.

question: What is the role of deep ploughing in wheat cultivation?
answer: Deep ploughing (30-35 cm) with disc plough: 1) Breaks hardpan (common in rice-wheat system). 2) Improves water infiltration and root penetration. 3) Exposes soil pests (termites) to predators. 4) Incorporates crop residues. 5) Reduces weed seed bank. Do once every 3-4 years.

question: What is the recommended land leveling (Laser Leveling) method before planting wheat?
answer: Laser leveling is highly recommended. Benefits: 1) Uniform irrigation saves 20-30% water. 2) Improves germination uniformity. 3) Reduces weed patches. 4) Essential for rice-wheat system to manage water. Field leveled to ±1 cm variation. Service cost: Rs. 2000-3000/acre. Subsidy available.

question: Should ridges and furrows be made for wheat cultivation in Pakistan? How?
answer: Bed planting (ridges and furrows) is recommended for waterlogged areas and rice-wheat system. Method: 1) Make 60-70 cm wide beds with 2-3 rows per bed. 2) Row spacing 20-25 cm. 3) Furrow depth 15-20 cm. Benefits: saves 30-40% irrigation water reduces lodging improves root growth. Not essential for well-drained flat fields.

question: How should previously harvested crop residue be managed before planting wheat?
answer: Rice-wheat system: Use Happy Seeder or zero-till drill to sow wheat into standing rice stubble without burning. Conventional: incorporate stubble with disc harrow + cultivator. Avoid burning (pollution loss of organic matter). For cotton-wheat: shred cotton stalks and incorporate.

question: What pre-sowing irrigation (Raunni) is required for wheat land preparation?
answer: Pre-sowing irrigation (raunni) is given 15-20 days before sowing when soil moisture is low. Apply 3-4 acre-inches water. After irrigation: allow soil to reach field capacity then cultivate when moisture is at "good tilth" (soil crumbles but does not stick to tools). Essential for late sowing and rainfed areas.

question: What implements and machinery are used for land preparation for wheat in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Disc plough (deep ploughing). 2) Disc harrow (for rice stubble). 3) Cultivator (2-3 passes). 4) Rotavator (for fine seedbed - use sparingly). 5) Plank (for leveling). 6) Laser land leveler. 7) Zero-till drill. 8) Happy Seeder. 9) Bed planter.

question: How many days before sowing should land preparation begin for wheat?
answer: Start land preparation 15-20 days before sowing. Timeline: Day 1: deep ploughing (if needed). Day 2-5: first cultivation + planking. Day 7-10: second cultivation + planking. Day 12-14: pre-sowing irrigation (if needed). Day 15-18: final cultivation + planking. Day 18-20: sowing.

question: How does land preparation differ for irrigated vs. rainfed (Barani) wheat cultivation?
answer: Irrigated: finer seedbed laser leveling important pre-sowing irrigation optional. Rainfed (Barani): focus on moisture conservation - fewer cultivations (3-4 passes) deep ploughing for water storage no pre-sowing irrigation rougher seedbed to reduce evaporation mulching. Use drought-tolerant varieties (Chakwal-50).

question: What is the recommended seed rate (kg/acre) for wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Recommended seed rate: 50-60 kg/acre (1-1.25 maunds). For late sowing (Dec): increase to 65-75 kg. For rainfed: 55-65 kg. For bold-seeded varieties: 60-70 kg. For zero-till: increase by 10-15%. Use certified seed for best germination.

question: What is the optimum row spacing and plant spacing for wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Row spacing: 22.5-30 cm (9-12 inches). For bed planting: 60-70 cm beds with 2-3 rows (20-25 cm between rows). Plant to plant spacing: 2-3 cm after emergence (not thinned). Target plant population: 100-120 plants per square meter (400000-480000 plants/acre).

question: What is the recommended sowing depth for wheat seeds in Pakistan?
answer: Sowing depth: 3-5 cm (1.5-2 inches). In sandy soils: 5-6 cm. In heavy soils: 2-3 cm. Deeper than 6 cm reduces emergence. Shallower than 2 cm risks drying out or bird damage. Seed should be placed in moist soil.

question: What sowing method is best for wheat — broadcast (Chatha) drill dibbling or transplanting?
answer: Drill sowing is best: 1) Uniform depth and spacing. 2) Seed saving (20-30% less seed). 3) Better germination. 4) Easier weed control. 5) Higher yield (10-15% more). Broadcasting (chatha) is traditional but inefficient. Dibbling too labor intensive. Transplanting not practiced.

question: How should wheat be sown after a previous crop (e.g. rice-wheat or cotton-wheat system)?
answer: Rice-wheat system: Use zero-till drill or Happy Seeder to sow wheat immediately after rice harvest (Nov 10-30). For cotton-wheat: Sow by Nov 30 maximum. Use relay cropping: sow wheat 15 days before cotton harvest. Short-duration cotton varieties help timely wheat sowing.

question: Can wheat be sown using zero-till or minimum-till techniques in Pakistan?
answer: Yes zero-till is highly successful especially after rice. Benefits: 1) Saves 15-20 days and Rs. 3000-4000/acre land prep. 2) Sows earlier. 3) Moisture conservation. 4) Reduced weed pressure. Use zero-till drill with inverted T-type furrow opener. Happy Seeder technology allows sowing in standing rice stubble without burning.

question: What equipment or tools (Seed Drill Planter) are used for sowing wheat in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Conventional seed drill (most common) - 9-11 row. 2) Zero-till drill (for after rice). 3) Happy Seeder (for rice stubble). 4) Bed planter (for bed planting). 5) Broadcaster (chatha) - traditional. Calibrate drill for 50-60 kg/acre seed rate. Row spacing 22.5-30 cm.

question: What are all the major crop management activities for wheat from sowing to harvest?
answer: Timeline: 0-10 days: sowing seed treatment. 10-25 days: germination check gap filling. 25-35 days: first irrigation + top dressing N + first weeding. 35-50 days: second weeding inter-cultivation. 50-65 days: second irrigation + second top dressing N. 65-80 days: third irrigation (flowering) - pest/disease monitoring. 80-100 days: grain filling - fourth irrigation if needed. 100-120 days: maturity - stop irrigation. 120-140 days: harvest.

question: What is the complete activity calendar (timeline) for wheat cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: October: land preparation (15-30 Oct). November: sowing (1-25 Nov). November-December: germination emergence (15 Nov-10 Dec) first irrigation (20-30 Nov). December: first weeding (1-15 Dec) inter-cultivation (15-31 Dec). January: second irrigation + top dressing (1-15 Jan) second weeding (15-31 Jan). February: third irrigation (1-15 Feb) flowering (15-28 Feb) pest monitoring. March: grain filling (1-31 Mar) fourth irrigation if needed. April-May: harvest (15 Apr-15 May).

question: When should thinning (Gidai) be done in wheat cultivation and how?
answer: Thinning is generally NOT practiced for wheat because seed rate is calibrated to achieve desired plant density. If overcrowding occurs due to excessive seed rate: no thinning (wheat tillers adjust). If poor emergence: gap filling may be done but not common.

question: When should earthing up (Mitti charhana) be done for wheat and why?
answer: Earthing up is generally not required for wheat. On bed planting systems: soil may be pulled from furrows to beds (earthing) at 30-35 days. Benefits: supports stems prevents lodging covers weeds. Not practiced in flat sowing.

question: How should inter-cultivation (Godi) be done in wheat fields?
answer: Inter-cultivation at 25-30 days and 40-45 days after sowing (before canopy closes). Method: 1) Use hand hoe (khurpa) or wheel hoe. 2) Cultivate between rows at 3-5 cm depth. 3) Avoid damaging roots. 4) Also breaks soil crust removes weeds aerates soil. For large areas: use cultivator with adjustable tines set to avoid plants. Common in irrigated areas.

question: What is the process of transplanting wheat seedlings (if applicable) and when should it be done?
answer: Transplanting is NOT practiced for wheat. Wheat is always direct seeded. Transplanting would damage the fibrous root system and is not economical.

question: What is the optimal plant population per acre for wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Optimal plant population: 400000-480000 plants per acre (100-120 plants per square meter). Achieved by: seed rate 50-60 kg/acre. Higher population causes lodging and more disease. Lower population reduces yield (fewer tillers).

question: How is gap filling done in wheat cultivation if germination is poor?
answer: Gap filling at 10-15 days after sowing. Method: 1) Pre-soak seeds overnight (for gap filling only). 2) Dibble 3-4 seeds per gap (missing plant area). 3) Irrigate lightly after gap filling. 4) If gaps >30%: consider replanting (if early enough). Use same variety as original sowing.

question: When and how should staking or support be provided to wheat plants?
answer: Staking is not required for wheat. Wheat stems are self-supporting. Lodging prevention: avoid excess N use lodging-resistant varieties (Punjab-2011) plant on beds.

question: What is pinching or pruning in wheat and when should it be done?
answer: Pinching (removal of apical meristem) is NOT recommended for wheat. It reduces yield. Wheat naturally stops growth after flowering.

question: How should wheat be managed during flowering to maximize fruit/grain set?
answer: 1) Ensure adequate soil moisture (irrigate if dry). 2) Avoid pesticide sprays during peak flowering (9 AM-4 PM) to protect pollinators (wheat is self-pollinated but bees may visit). 3) Provide boron (foliar 0.1% boric acid) at booting if deficient. 4) Protect from frost (irrigation before frost night). 5) Manage aphids (honeydew interferes with pollination). 6) Avoid overhead irrigation which washes pollen.

question: What is the process of ratooning (Munda) for wheat in Pakistan? Is it recommended?
answer: Ratooning is NOT recommended for wheat. Unlike sugarcane wheat does not regrow after harvest. Secondary growth is poor low yielding and disease-prone. Always plant fresh seed each season.

question: How does crop canopy management improve yield of wheat?
answer: Canopy management: 1) Optimum plant population (400000-480000 plants/acre) prevents overcrowding. 2) Proper row spacing (22.5-30 cm) allows light penetration. 3) Avoid excess N which causes dense canopy and lodging. 4) Inter-cultivation improves air circulation reducing disease (rust powdery mildew). Good canopy = balanced tillering + high grain yield.

question: What field monitoring activities should a farmer do weekly during wheat season?
answer: Weekly monitoring: 1) Germination % (first 2 weeks). 2) Plant stand and gaps. 3) Tillering count (30-45 days). 4) Weed presence and type. 5) Pest scouting: aphids (check under leaves and on heads) jassids. 6) Disease signs: rust (orange/brown pustules on leaves) powdery mildew (white powder) karnal bunt (black powder in heads). 7) Nutrient deficiency symptoms. 8) Soil moisture. Record observations.

question: What are the most commonly grown varieties of wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Commonly grown varieties include: 1) Galaxy-2013 (high yield 55-65 maunds/acre). 2) Faisalabad-2008 (rust tolerant). 3) Sehar-2006 (heat tolerant for late sowing). 4) Punjab-2011 (drought and heat tolerant). 5) Millat-2020 (new high yielder). 6) Inqalab-91 (older but widely adapted). 7) Chakwal-50 (rainfed). 8) Benazir-2013 (for Sindh). 9) Zincol-2016 (zinc biofortified).

question: What are the improved and recommended varieties of wheat approved by Pakistani agricultural research institutes?
answer: Improved varieties approved by PARC/NARC/Ayub Research/AARI: 1) Galaxy-2013 (Ayub Research) - high yield 55-65 maunds/acre rust resistant. 2) Millat-2020 (AARI) - triple rust resistance yield 60+ maunds. 3) Faisalabad-2008 (AARI) - leaf rust tolerant. 4) Punjab-2011 (AARI) - heat and drought tolerant. 5) Sehar-2006 (NARC) - heat tolerant for late sowing. 6) Zincol-2016 (NARC/AARI) - zinc biofortified. 7) Akbar-2019 (NARC) - drought tolerant. 8) Benazir-2013 (Sindh) - heat tolerant for Sindh. 9) Kiran-95 (salt tolerant). 10) Chakwal-50 (Barani) - drought tolerant for rainfed.

question: What are the early-maturing medium-maturing and late-maturing varieties of wheat available in Pakistan?
answer: Early-maturing (130-140 days): Sehar-2006 Ujala-2016 AARI-2011. Medium-maturing (140-150 days): Galaxy-2013 Faisalabad-2008 Punjab-2011 Millat-2020. Late-maturing (150-160 days): Inqalab-91 local landraces. Early varieties suit rice-wheat system and late sowing. Late varieties for full-season irrigated areas.

question: What are the drought-tolerant varieties of wheat recommended for rainfed areas of Pakistan?
answer: 1) Chakwal-50 (Barani) - high yield under drought. 2) Dharabi-2011 (NARC) - drought tolerant. 3) Fatehjang-16 (short duration). 4) NARC-2009 (rainfed). 5) Akbar-2019 (drought tolerant). 6) Local landraces from Pothwar. These varieties have deeper roots earlier maturity and osmotic adjustment. Yield under rainfed: 15-25 maunds/acre.

question: What heat-tolerant varieties of wheat are suitable for hot regions like Sindh and South Punjab?
answer: 1) Sehar-2006 (heat tolerant for late sowing). 2) Benazir-2013 (Sindh). 3) NARC-2011 (terminal heat). 4) Mairaj-2008 (temperature up to 35°C). 5) Punjab-2011 (moderate tolerance). 6) Galaxy-2013 (good for central Punjab). Key management: early sowing (Nov 1-15) to complete grain filling before March heat.

question: What high-yielding varieties of wheat give the best production in Pakistan?
answer: Highest yielders: Galaxy-2013 (55-65 maunds/acre). Millat-2020 (60+ maunds). Faisalabad-2008 (50-60 maunds). Anaj-2017 (50-55 maunds). Ujala-2016 (50-60 maunds). Pakistan-2013 (50-55 maunds). Also Zincol-2016 (zinc enriched 50-55 maunds).

question: What type of soil is best suited for growing wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Well-drained loamy or clay loam soil rich in organic matter is best. Deep fertile soils (45-60 cm depth) with pH 6.0-7.5. Wheat tolerates a range of soils from sandy loam to clay loam. Avoid waterlogged and highly saline soils. Heavy clays require careful water management.

question: What is the ideal soil pH range for wheat cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Ideal pH range is 6.0 to 7.5 (neutral to slightly alkaline). Wheat can tolerate pH 5.5-8.5 but yields decline below 5.5 (Al toxicity) and above 8.5 (micronutrient deficiency). At pH >8.0: iron and zinc deficiency common.

question: What soil texture (loamy sandy clayey) is most suitable for wheat?
answer: Clay loam and loam are most suitable - provide good water holding capacity and nutrient retention. Sandy soils: require frequent irrigation and high fertilizer. Clay soils: good fertility but risk of waterlogging if drainage poor.

question: Can wheat be grown on saline or sodic soils (Kallar) in Pakistan? What are the precautions?
answer: Wheat has moderate salt tolerance (ECe up to 6-8 dS/m for yield reduction <25%). On saline/sodic soils: 1) Apply gypsum at 50-100% GR based on soil test. 2) Use salt-tolerant varieties (Kiran-95 LU-26 SARC-1). 3) Pre-sowing leaching with 6-8 acre-inches good water. 4) Add FYM 10-12 tons/acre. 5) Avoid saline irrigation water (EC >2 dS/m).

question: What soil drainage conditions are required for wheat?
answer: Moderate to good drainage is essential. Wheat can tolerate brief waterlogging but standing water for >48 hours causes root damage and yellowing. Clay soils require proper leveling and drainage channels. Rice-wheat system soils often have drainage issues.

question: How does soil organic matter content affect the yield of wheat?
answer: Higher organic matter (1-2%) improves: 1) Water holding capacity (critical in rainfed). 2) Nutrient availability (especially N and P). 3) Soil structure and root penetration. 4) Beneficial microbial activity. Every 0.5% increase in OM can boost yield by 2-3 maunds/acre.

question: What soil testing should a farmer do before planting wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Essential soil tests: 1) pH and EC (salinity). 2) Organic matter. 3) Available N (NO3-N). 4) Available P (Olsen P). 5) Available K. 6) Zinc (Zn) - very common deficiency. 7) Boron (B) in sandy soils. Sample depth: 6-9 inches. Send to provincial soil testing lab (free or low cost).

question: How should soil fertility be maintained or improved for repeated cultivation of wheat?
answer: 1) Crop rotation: wheat after legumes (mungbean gram) or fallow. 2) Apply FYM/compost 8-10 tons/acre every 2-3 years. 3) Green manuring (dhaincha) before wheat. 4) Balanced NPK fertilization (not just urea). 5) Incorporate crop residues (wheat stubble). 6) Use biofertilizers (PSB for phosphorus).

question: What are the signs of poor or unsuitable soil for wheat cultivation?
answer: Signs: 1) Water pooling after irrigation (poor drainage). 2) White salt crust (saline). 3) Stunted yellow plants (N deficiency or waterlogging). 4) Purple leaf tips (P deficiency). 5) Yellowing between veins (Zn deficiency). 6) Poor root development (compacted soil).

question: What soil preparation practices improve the structure and health of soil for wheat?
answer: 1) Deep ploughing (30-35 cm) every 3-4 years to break hardpan. 2) Add organic matter (FYM 8-10 tons/acre). 3) Green manuring 6-8 weeks before sowing. 4) Gypsum application for sodic soils. 5) Laser leveling for uniform irrigation and drainage. 6) Zero-till or minimum-till in rice-wheat system.

question: When is the best time to sow wheat in Punjab Pakistan?
answer: Optimum sowing: October 25 to November 25. Central Punjab: Oct 25-Nov 20. South Punjab (Multan Bahawalpur): Nov 1-25. North Punjab (Rawalpindi): Oct 15-Nov 15. Early sowing (Oct) increases rust risk. Late sowing (Dec) reduces yield by 1-1.5% per day.

question: When is the best time to sow wheat in Sindh Pakistan?
answer: Sindh: November 1 to November 30. Lower Sindh (Hyderabad): Nov 1-20. Upper Sindh (Sukkur): Nov 10-30. Use short-duration varieties if sowing after December. Sukkur region: best sowing Nov 15-25.

question: When is the best time to sow wheat in KPK Pakistan?
answer: KPK: October 20 to November 15. Peshawar valley: Oct 25-Nov 15. Dera Ismail Khan: Nov 1-20. Higher elevations (Swat Abbottabad): Oct 15-30. Use cold-tolerant varieties for late sowing.

question: When is the best time to sow wheat in Balochistan Pakistan?
answer: Balochistan: October 15 to November 20. Quetta region: Oct 15-30. Sibi/Naseerabad: Nov 1-20. Use drought-tolerant varieties for rainfed areas (e.g. NARC-2009).

question: When is the best time to sow wheat in South Punjab (Multan Bahawalpur DG Khan)?
answer: South Punjab: November 1 to November 25. Warmer winter allows later sowing. Sow by Nov 25 maximum. Delay reduces yield 1-1.5% per day.

question: What happens if wheat is sown too early or too late in Pakistan?
answer: Too early (September-early October): 1) High temperatures (>30°C) reduce germination. 2) Vegetative growth excessive. 3) Higher risk of yellow rust. 4) More pest pressure (aphids). Too late (December onward): 1) Shortened growing season. 2) Heat stress during grain filling - shriveled grain. 3) Lower yield (1-1.5% loss per day). 4) Higher seed rate required.

question: How does sowing time affect the yield and quality of wheat?
answer: Yield: Each week delay after Nov 15 reduces yield by 5-10%. Optimum Nov sowing gives 50-60 maunds/acre. December sowing gives 30-40 maunds. Quality: Late sowing produces shriveled grains with lower protein content. Early sowing (Oct) may give good yield but higher rust risk.

question: What seed treatment (Zahar-alood) should be done before sowing wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Seed treatment is essential: 1) Fungicide for seed-borne diseases (karnal bunt loose smut). 2) Insecticide for termites and early aphids. 3) Bio-fertilizer (optional). Treat seeds 24-48 hours before sowing. Use 20-30 ml water per kg seed.

question: Which fungicide is recommended for seed treatment of wheat to prevent soil-borne diseases?
answer: Recommended fungicides: 1) Carbendazim (Bavistin) 2g per kg seed. 2) Thiram 2.5g per kg seed. 3) Tebuconazole (Raxil) 1.5ml per kg seed. 4) Vitavax (Carboxin) 2g per kg for loose smut and karnal bunt. For severe disease history: double dose.

question: Which insecticide is recommended for seed treatment of wheat to protect against early pests?
answer: 1) Imidacloprid (Confidor) 5ml per kg seed - controls early aphids and termites up to 30 days. 2) Chlorpyrifos 2-3ml per kg - for termites. 3) Thiamethoxam (Cruiser) 4ml per kg - broad spectrum.

question: What is the process of seed treatment for wheat — dose method and timing?
answer: Process: 1) Calculate seed quantity (50-60 kg/acre). 2) Mix required fungicide + insecticide in 1-1.5 liters water per 50 kg seed. 3) Spread seeds on clean polythene sheet. 4) Pour solution gradually while mixing manually (wear gloves). 5) Ensure uniform coating. 6) Dry in shade for 1-2 hours (not direct sun). 7) Sow within 24-48 hours.

question: Should wheat seeds be soaked in water before sowing? For how long?
answer: Soaking is not recommended for wheat. Soaked seeds may rot in cold soil and are difficult to drill. Dry seed treatment followed by direct sowing is best.

question: How does seed treatment affect germination rate and early growth of wheat?
answer: Seed treatment increases germination from 70-80% (untreated) to 90-95% (treated). It protects seedlings from soil-borne pathogens (damping off) and early pests. Treated seeds establish faster more uniform stands and have better root development. Result: 10-15% higher yield potential.

question: What is bio-priming or microbial seed treatment for wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Bio-priming involves treating seeds with beneficial microbes: 1) Azotobacter or Azospirillum (N-fixers) - 1 packet (500g) for 15-20 kg seed. 2) PSB (Phosphorus Solubilizing Bacteria) - 1 packet for 15 kg seed. 3) Trichoderma harzianum (bio-fungicide) - 5g per kg seed. Mix with jaggery solution (50g jaggery in 1L water) as adhesive. Dry in shade. Reduces chemical fertilizer need by 15-25%.

question: How should treated wheat seed be stored before sowing?
answer: Treated seeds should be sown within 24-48 hours maximum. Do not store treated seeds for more than 7 days as fungicides degrade. If storage unavoidable: keep in cool dry place in breathable (not plastic) bags. Never mix treated seeds with untreated seeds.

question: What are the safety precautions when doing seed treatment for wheat?
answer: 1) Wear gloves and mask. 2) Do not eat/drink during treatment. 3) Treat in well-ventilated area. 4) Wash hands thoroughly after treatment. 5) Keep treated seed away from children and livestock. 6) Dispose empty chemical containers properly (triple rinse then crush). 7) Do not use treated seed for consumption or feed.

question: What are the major weeds (Khar-palwar) found in wheat fields in Pakistan?
answer: Major weeds: Broadleaf: 1) Bathu (Chenopodium album). 2) Maina (Asphodelus tenuifolius). 3) Peeli Buti (Fumaria parviflora). 4) Lehli (Sonchus asper). 5) Jangli palak (Rumex dentatus). 6) Kandiar (Convolvulus arvensis). Grasses: 1) Wild oat (Avena fatua) - most problematic. 2) Phalaris minor (Dumbi sitti) - resistant to many herbicides. 3) Cyperus rotundus (Deela). 4) Cynodon dactylon (Khabbal grass).

question: What is the critical period of weed competition in wheat cultivation?
answer: Critical period: 15 to 60 days after sowing (from tillering to flowering). Weeds competing during this period cause 40-70% yield loss. First 30 days are most critical. Keep weed-free during this window. After 60 days wheat canopy closes and suppresses late weeds.

question: How does weed competition affect the yield of wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Weed competition can reduce yield by 40-70%. Heavy infestation: yield drop from 50 maunds to 15-20 maunds/acre. Grassy weeds (wild oat Phalaris) are more damaging than broadleaf. Weeds compete for water (critical in rainfed) nutrients (especially N) light and space. Also harbor pests (aphids) and diseases (rust).

question: What are the recommended herbicides (Zahar) for weed control in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Broadleaf weeds: Buctril M (Bromoxynil+MCPA) 400ml/acre Starane M (Fluroxypyr) 300ml/acre Logran (Triasulfuron) 200g/acre 24-D Na salt 600g/acre. 2) Grassy weeds: Puma Super (Fenoxaprop) 500ml/acre Axial (Pinoxaden) 300ml/acre Atlantis (Mesosulfuron+Iodosulfuron) 14.4g/acre. Apply at 30-40 days after sowing.

question: What pre-emergence herbicides are used for wheat weed control?
answer: Pre-emergence (apply within 3 days of sowing before weed emergence): 1) Pendimethalin (Stomp) 500-600ml/acre - effective on grasses and small-seeded broadleaf weeds. 2) Trifluralin (Treflan) 400-500ml/acre - incorporate into top 5-8 cm soil within 24 hours. Apply on moist soil. Do not use on sandy soils (leaching risk).

question: What post-emergence herbicides are used for wheat weed control?
answer: Post-emergence (apply at 25-40 days after sowing at 3-4 leaf stage of weeds): For broadleaf weeds: Buctril M 400ml/acre Starane M 300ml/acre 24-D 600g/acre (avoid before tillering - causes twisting). For grassy weeds: Puma Super 500ml/acre (wild oat) Axial 300ml/acre Atlantis 14.4g/acre (Phalaris resistant strains).

question: What is the correct dose and timing of herbicide application in wheat?
answer: Pendimethalin: 500-600 ml/acre within 3 days of sowing. Puma Super: 500ml/acre at 30-40 days (wild oat 3-4 leaf). Axial: 300ml/acre. Buctril M: 400ml/acre at 30-40 days. 24-D: 600g/acre at 35-45 days (after tillering). Use 100-120 liters water/acre. Flat fan nozzle. Apply in morning when no wind/rain forecast. Temperature 15-25°C.

question: How should manual weeding (Khurpa/Godi) be done in wheat fields?
answer: Manual weeding: 1st weeding at 20-25 days (after first irrigation). 2nd weeding at 40-45 days (before canopy closure). Method: 1) Use khurpa (hand hoe) to cut weeds just below soil surface. 2) Remove weeds from field (don't leave uprooted weeds). 3) Be careful not to disturb wheat roots. 4) Weeding also aerates soil. Labor requirement: 15-20 person-days/acre for two weedings.

question: How many manual weedings are recommended for wheat cultivation in Pakistan?
answer: Two manual weedings are recommended: 1st at 20-25 days after sowing. 2nd at 40-45 days after sowing. In low weed pressure areas: one weeding at 25-30 days may suffice. In heavy weed infestation: two weedings + pre-emergence herbicide. Rainfed areas: timely weeding critical due to limited moisture.

question: What mechanical methods (Weeders) can be used for weed control in wheat?
answer: 1) Wheel hoe (hand-operated) - for row spacing 22.5-30 cm. 2) Tractor-drawn cultivator with adjustable tines - for large fields (set to avoid plant rows). 3) Cono-weeder (for narrow rows). Mechanical weeding at 25-30 and 40-45 days. Inter-cultivation should be shallow (3-5 cm) to avoid root damage. Followed by manual removal of intra-row weeds.

question: How can mulching help control weeds in wheat cultivation?
answer: Mulching is not common for wheat but effective in rainfed areas: 1) Straw mulch (previous crop residue) at 2-3 tons/acre - suppresses weeds. 2) Reduces weed germination by blocking light. 3) Also conserves soil moisture (valuable for rainfed). 4) Zero-till wheat with residue retention (Happy Seeder) provides natural mulch. 5) Plastic mulch not economical for wheat.

question: What safety precautions should be taken when applying herbicides to wheat?
answer: 1) Wear PPE (gloves mask goggles). 2) Read label instructions. 3) Calibrate sprayer correctly. 4) Do not spray on windy days (drift damages nearby crops especially cotton/vegetables from 24-D). 5) Avoid application before rain. 6) Clean equipment thoroughly after use. 7) Dispose containers properly. 8) Observe pre-harvest interval (PHI - usually 30-40 days). 9) Do not enter field for 24 hours after spraying.

question: What are the major insect pests of wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Major pests: 1) Wheat aphid (Rhopalosiphum padi Schizaphis graminum Sitobion avenae) - most damaging. 2) Armyworm (Spodoptera exigua). 3) Cutworm (Agrotis spp.) - seedling stage. 4) Wheat stem borer (rare). 5) Termites (Microtermes spp.) - in rainfed areas. 6) Jassids (Amrasca spp.). 7) Whitefly (occasional).

question: What is the economic threshold level (ETL) for major pests of wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Aphids: 10-15 per tiller or 20% plants infested (at flowering). Armyworm: 3-4 larvae per square meter. Cutworm: 2-3 cut seedlings per square meter. Termites: 5-10% plants infested. Spray only when ETL reached (avoid unnecessary pesticides to protect natural enemies).

question: How can I identify sucking pests (aphids whitefly thrips jassids) attacking wheat?
answer: Aphids: Small (2-3mm) pear-shaped green/brown/black insects in colonies on leaves stems and developing grain heads. Sticky honeydew + sooty mold. Whitefly: Tiny white winged insects fly when plant disturbed (rare in wheat). Thrips: Tiny (1mm) slender insects. Silvery streaks on leaves. Jassids: Pale green wedge-shaped insects. Leaves curl downward with white edges.

question: What damage does the stem borer cause to wheat and how to identify it?
answer: Stem borer is rare in wheat but occasional. Damage: Larva bores into stem causing wilting of terminal shoot (dead heart). Plant may break at bored point. Identification: Small hole near base frass (sawdust) around hole. Control: Remove and destroy affected plants. Not common in Pakistan wheat.

question: What damage does the fruit borer / bollworm cause to wheat and how to identify it?
answer: Wheat does not have fruit. Bollworm is not a pest of wheat.

question: What damage does the leaf miner cause to wheat and how to identify it?
answer: Leaf miner is not a major pest of wheat. Occasional on young leaves - winding white mines. Not economically significant.

question: What damage do armyworms / cutworms cause to wheat seedlings in Pakistan?
answer: Cutworms: Larvae cut seedlings at ground level at night. Damage: Plants fall over as if cut by knife. Patchy missing plants. Armyworms: Defoliation - skeletonized leaves. Large larvae eat entire leaves. Identification: Larvae curled (C-shape) when disturbed in soil near damaged plants. Control: Chlorpyrifos drench around base.

question: What damage does the whitefly cause to wheat and how to identify infestation?
answer: Whitefly is not a major pest of wheat in Pakistan. Occasional in warmer areas. Damage: 1) Suck sap causing yellowing and stunting. 2) Honeydew leads to sooty mold. Identification: Tiny white moths fly up when plant disturbed.

question: What damage does the red spider mite cause to wheat and when does it appear?
answer: Red spider mite is rare in wheat. Appears in dry hot conditions (Feb-March late season). Damage: Stippling (tiny yellow/white spots) on leaves. Fine webbing. Identification: Tiny red dots visible with hand lens. Control: Abamectin if severe.

question: How do locusts and grasshoppers damage wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Locusts (desert locust) and grasshoppers: 1) Defoliation - eat entire leaves and stems. 2) Can completely destroy crop in hours during swarms. 3) Grasshoppers cause irregular chewing damage. Identification: Presence of insects. Droppings on leaves. Control: Chlorpyrifos or Deltamethrin. District agriculture department issues alerts.

question: What are the signs of termite infestation in wheat fields?
answer: Signs: 1) Dried dead plants that pull out easily with no roots. 2) Mud tubes on plant stems near base. 3) Hollowed stems. 4) White/cream insects inside roots/stem when dug up. 5) Patchy plant death. More common in rainfed areas and fields with crop residues. Control: Chlorpyrifos seed treatment or soil drench.

question: What are the signs of nematode infestation in wheat roots in Pakistan?
answer: Cereal cyst nematode (Heterodera avenae): Signs: 1) Stunted yellow patches in field. 2) Poor root development with cysts (white/yellow pinhead size). 3) Reduced tillering. More common in sandy soils and rainfed areas. Control: crop rotation (with non-host crops) resistant varieties.

question: How does the pest population in wheat vary across different regions of Pakistan?
answer: Aphids: Severe in all wheat areas - peak February-March. Armyworm: More in central Punjab and KPK. Cutworms: Problem in rainfed areas (Pothwar). Termites: More in sandy and low organic matter soils (Thal Cholistan). Nematodes: More in rainfed areas and sandy soils.

question: What pests are more severe for wheat during the Kharif season?
answer: Wheat is not grown in Kharif (summer). Pests that persist in off-season: aphids and armyworm may survive on grasses.

question: What pests are more severe for wheat during the Rabi season?
answer: Rabi (winter) pests: Aphids (most severe Nov-Apr). Armyworm (Feb-Mar). Cutworms (Nov-Dec on seedlings). Termites (throughout). Aphid population peaks in February-March.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling aphids in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Imidacloprid (Confidor) 250ml/acre. 2) Thiamethoxam (Actara) 80g/acre. 3) Acetamiprid 200g/acre. 4) Dimethoate (Rogor) 400ml/acre. 5) Malathion 500ml/acre (less toxic to natural enemies). 6) Pirimicarb (Aphox) - specific for aphids. Spray when ETL reached (10-15 aphids/tiller). Alternate products to avoid resistance.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling whitefly in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Whitefly is not a major pest of wheat. If infestation occurs: Imidacloprid 250ml/acre or Diafenthiuron 300ml/acre.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling thrips in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Thrips are rare in wheat. If needed: Spinosad 80ml/acre.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling stem borer in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Stem borer rare. If present: Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre. Remove and destroy infested plants.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling fruit borer/bollworm in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Not applicable (wheat has no fruit).

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling leaf miner in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Not a major pest. If needed: Abamectin 200ml/acre.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling red spider mite in wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Rare. If needed: Abamectin 200ml/acre or Sulfur 80% WP 500g/acre.

question: What pesticides are recommended for controlling cutworm/armyworm in wheat seedlings?
answer: 1) Chlorpyrifos (Lorsban) 800ml/acre - soil drench around base. 2) Lambda-cyhalothrin 250ml/acre - evening spray. 3) Carbaryl (Sevin) 400g/acre. 4) Bait: Mix 1kg bran + 10g Carbaryl + 1L water - spread in evening. Apply when cutting damage first seen. Remove weeds around field (alternate hosts).

question: What is the recommended dose and spray schedule for pesticide application on wheat?
answer: Aphids: Spray when 10-15/tiller or 20% infested. Schedule: Feb-Mar (peak). Armyworm: spray when larvae seen. Use 100-120 L water/acre. Rotate pesticides every 15-20 days. Stop spraying 14 days before harvest (PHI).

question: How should pesticides be mixed and applied correctly for wheat pest control?
answer: 1) Fill spray tank 1/3 with clean water. 2) Add required pesticide dose (measure accurately). 3) Add adjuvant/wetter if recommended. 4) Fill to full volume while agitating. 5) Calibrate sprayer for 100-120 L/acre. 6) Use flat fan or hollow cone nozzles. 7) Spray in morning (6-9 AM) or evening (4-7 PM). 8) Avoid windy/rainy conditions. 9) Clean sprayer after use.

question: What is the pre-harvest interval (PHI) for pesticides used on wheat in Pakistan?
answer: Common PHI: Imidacloprid: 14 days. Thiamethoxam: 14 days. Dimethoate: 14 days. Chlorpyrifos: 15 days. Lambda-cyhalothrin: 14 days. Malathion: 7 days. Do not harvest or graze animals on wheat before PHI. Check product label for specific PHI.

question: What are the bio-pesticides or organic alternatives for pest control in wheat?
answer: 1) Neem oil (Azadirachtin) 1% - 2-3 L/acre for aphids. 2) Garlic-chili extract (10g garlic + 10g chili in 1L water boil strain dilute 1:10). 3) Tobacco extract (100g tobacco in 1L water soak 24h strain) - effective for aphids but toxic to humans. 4) Entomopathogenic fungi: Beauveria bassiana for aphids. 5) Yellow sticky traps for aphids.

question: How can pheromone traps be used for pest monitoring in wheat fields?
answer: For armyworm: Use pheromone lures in delta traps (1 trap per 2 acres). For cutworm: use specific lures. Place traps at canopy height (30-40 cm). Check daily for moth catch. Spray when catch exceeds threshold (e.g. 8-10 moths/trap/night). Replace lures every 4-6 weeks.

question: What safety equipment should a farmer wear while spraying pesticide on wheat?
answer: 1) Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile rubber). 2) Face shield or goggles. 3) Respirator (N95 or charcoal mask for organic vapors). 4) Long-sleeved shirt and full pants. 5) Apron or coverall. 6) Rubber boots (not cloth shoes). 7) Hat. Wash PPE after use. Never reuse empty pesticide containers. Shower after spraying.

question: What should a farmer do if accidental pesticide poisoning occurs during wheat spraying?
answer: 1) Remove person from contaminated area immediately. 2) Remove contaminated clothing. 3) Wash skin with soap and water for 15 minutes. 4) If swallowed: Do not induce vomiting (unless label says) - give water. 5) If inhaled: Move to fresh air. 6) Take pesticide container to hospital (for identification). 7) Seek immediate medical attention. 8) Call Poison Control (115 or local emergency).

question: How should pesticide resistance be managed in wheat pests in Pakistan?
answer: 1) Rotate pesticides with different modes of action (IRAC groups). 2) Do not use same pesticide group repeatedly. 3) Spray only when ETL reached (not calendar-based). 4) Use recommended doses (not sub-lethal). 5) Integrate biological and cultural controls (IPM). 6) Leave untreated refuges (unsprayed areas) for susceptible pests. 7) Use pheromone traps for monitoring.

question: When is the best time of day (morning/evening) to spray pesticide on wheat?
answer: Best time: Early morning (6-9 AM) or late evening (4-7 PM). Reasons: 1) Bees and pollinators less active (protect beneficials). 2) Temperature moderate (15-25°C) - better efficacy. 3) Less evaporation. 4) Lower wind speeds. Avoid spraying: 1) Mid-day heat (>30°C). 2) Strong wind (>15 km/h). 3) When rain expected within 6 hours. 4) When leaves are wet (dew/rain).

question: What integrated pest management (IPM) practices are recommended for wheat in Pakistan?
answer: IPM components: 1) Use resistant varieties (for rust). 2) Crop rotation (3-4 years with non-cereals). 3) Clean seed (certified disease-free). 4) Balanced fertilizer (no excess N). 5) Optimum plant population (avoid dense canopy). 6) Monitoring (weekly scouting). 7) Economic thresholds (spray only when needed). 8) Biological control (conserve ladybirds lacewings). 9) Selective pesticides. 10) Sanitation (remove crop debris).

question: How can crop rotation help reduce pests and diseases in wheat cultivation?
answer: Crop rotation breaks pest/disease cycles: 1) Wheat after legumes (gram mungbean) - adds N reduces diseases. 2) Avoid wheat after wheat (minimum 1-2 years) to reduce rust and smut inoculum. 3) Rotate with non-host crops: maize sorghum mustard. 4) Reduces cereal cyst nematode. 5) Improves soil health. Sample rotation: Wheat - fallow - gram - wheat.

question: How does selection of disease-resistant wheat varieties reduce losses in Pakistan?
answer: Resistant varieties (Millat-2020 Aas-2011) provide: 1) 80-90% reduction in rust severity. 2) No need for fungicide sprays (saves Rs. 2000-3000/acre). 3) Higher yield (55-65 vs 40-45 maunds). 4) Better grain quality. 5) Reduced inoculum for neighboring fields. Always use resistant varieties where available.

question: What cultural practices help prevent pest attacks on wheat?
answer: 1) Timely sowing (Nov 1-15) - avoids peak aphid and rust seasons. 2) Avoid excess nitrogen (lush growth attracts aphids and rust). 3) Proper spacing (22.5-30 cm) - air circulation reduces disease. 4) Weed control (weeds host aphids). 5) Remove crop debris after harvest. 6) Deep ploughing in summer (exposes pupae). 7) Balanced irrigation (no waterlogging).

question: How does field sanitation (removing crop debris) prevent disease in wheat?
answer: 1) Removes rust-infected plant material (overwintering inoculum). 2) Reduces smut and bunt survival structures. 3) Removes volunteer wheat plants (alternative hosts for rust). 4) Destroys pest hiding places (cutworms). 5) Practice: After harvest collect and burn or deep plough (>30cm) wheat stubble. Do not compost infected debris. Clean cultivation equipment between fields.

question: How can border cropping or trap cropping reduce pests in wheat fields?
answer: Border crop: Surround wheat field with 2-3 rows of mustard or barley. Mustard attracts aphids away from wheat (trap crop). When border crop is infested with aphids spray only the border (not main crop). Reduces pesticide use by 50-70%. Barley as border reduces rust spread.

question: What beneficial insects should be protected to help control pests in wheat?
answer: Beneficial insects: 1) Ladybird beetles (Coccinella) - eat aphids (up to 50/day). 2) Lacewings (Chrysoperla) - larvae eat aphids. 3) Syrphid flies (hoverflies) - larvae eat aphids. 4) Parasitic wasps (Aphidius) - parasitize aphids. 5) Spiders - generalist predators. 6) Ground beetles - eat cutworms. Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides (pyrethroids organophosphates) to conserve them.

question: How does proper irrigation management reduce disease risk in wheat?
answer: 1) Avoid over-irrigation - reduces humidity and rust/mildew. 2) Furrow irrigation (not flood) - keeps foliage drier. 3) Irrigate in morning - leaves dry by evening. 4) Avoid waterlogging - reduces root rot. 5) Stop irrigation 2 weeks before harvest - prevents late season disease. Wet foliage + cool nights = disease explosion.

question: How does proper fertilizer management help prevent disease in wheat?
answer: 1) Balanced NPK (not excess N) - excess N causes lush growth dense canopy high humidity more rust/mildew and more aphids. 2) Adequate P and K - strengthen cell walls improve disease resistance. 3) Apply K (potassium) - reduces rust severity. 4) Micronutrients (Zn) - prevent stress-induced susceptibility. 5) Organic matter (FYM) - improves soil health and beneficial microbes.

question: What is the role of light traps and pheromone traps in wheat pest management?
answer: Light traps: 1) Attract night-flying pests (armyworm cutworm moths). 2) Place 1 trap per 2 acres. 3) Operate from dusk to dawn. 4) Helps monitor pest emergence. Pheromone traps: 1) Species-specific (e.g. armyworm). 2) 1 trap per 2 acres. 3) Count moths daily. 4) Spray when catch exceeds threshold. Both are monitoring tools not direct control.

question: How should wheat fields be monitored regularly to catch pest/disease problems early?
